records.content: News Around the World University students were the first to spread new SARS-CoV-2 variants — Nature Fedir Kryshtovskyi 19 November 2026 20:44 In Massachusetts, an analysis of more than 85,000 SARS-CoV-2 genome sequences showed that university students consistently began spreading new genetic variants of the virus first. The highest level of COVID-19 transmission in 2021–2023 was also recorded among school students aged 15–18 and residents of elderly care facilities. Testing data in Massachusetts As Nature reports, researchers combined genomic data with epidemiological information about people with COVID-19, including their age and vaccination status. They used test results collected in Massachusetts from November 2021 to January 2023. Genome sequencing made it possible to track the spread of SARS-CoV-2 variants that emerged during this period. More current news is available on the UA.News Telegram channel Telegram . Risks for workers At the same time, employees of schools, universities and elderly care facilities had approximately the same risk of contracting COVID-19 as people in the communities surrounding these institutions. The authors of the analysis also found that booster vaccinations reduced the transmission of SARS-CoV-2, including the Omicron BA.1 variant, which began circulating in Massachusetts in late 2021. The study results were published on November 19, 2026, in the journal Cell. Epidemiologist Bill Hanage of the Harvard School of Public Health called the scale of the work an impressive example of the capabilities of population genomics. Read us on Download our app

records.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Monday, November 23, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Lower Neutralizing Antibodies Correlate With Protracted Illness in Longitudinal COVID-19 Study by November 21, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 6 mins read 0 Lower Neutralizing Antibodies Correlate With Protracted Illness in Longitudinal COVID-19 Study Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram A longitudinal study analyzing serum samples from COVID-19 patients at UCLA-affiliated hospitals has revealed significant correlations between host neutralizing antibody levels, clinical disease trajectories, and the ongoing evolutionary adaptations of SARS-CoV-2 variants. Researchers evaluated the neutralizing capacity of antibodies targeting the viral spike protein receptor-binding domain to track how humoral immunity interacts with viral mutation and patient outcomes across distinct pandemic waves. The investigation examined 305 longitudinal serum samples collected from 86 patients infected during the initial pre-vaccine wave, alongside cohorts of 20 individuals during the Omicron period and 18 individuals during the post-Omicron period. By deploying virus neutralization tests against the SARS-CoV-2 receptor-binding domain, the authors quantified neutralizing antibody inhibition scores across patient populations over extended timelines following confirmed infection. Discover more Book Care Services Find Therapists Get Health Tips Among the 86 first-wave patients, researchers evaluated 300 serum samples collected at various time points after infection and stratified antibody responses into percentile-based groups based on inhibition scores ranging from 1 to 100. The lower 25th percentile cohort, designated S25, comprised 29 patients who consistently exhibited low neutralization scores below 25, registering a median score of 7.46 with a 95 percent confidence interval from 6.1 to 8.8. Discover more Study Biology Track Biotech Check Symptoms COVID-19 The middle 50th percentile group, labeled S50, included 44 patients with intermediate neutralizing antibody scores falling between 25 and 75, exhibiting a median score of 45.77 and a 95 percent confidence interval from 39.5 to 52.1. The upper 75th percentile group, designated S75, consisted of 13 patients displaying consistently elevated neutralization scores above 75, with a median score of 88 and a 95 percent confidence interval from 75.95 to 85.52. Temporal analysis of humoral immunity demonstrated that peak neutralizing antibody activity occurred at a median of approximately 18 days following SARS-CoV-2 infection. Neutralization activity remained detectable in longitudinal patient sera past 100 days post-infection, establishing a clear baseline for tracking how antibody persistence correlates with long-term viral clearance and clinical progression. Hospital records revealed marked differences in healthcare utilization and symptom duration corresponding to these neutralizing antibody tiers. Patients in the low-antibody S25 group experienced a median of two hospital visits or admissions compared to a median of one visit among S75 patients. Furthermore, S25 patients had significantly longer hospitalizations with persistent COVID-19 symptoms, recording a median stay of 41 days compared to 31 days for the S75 group. Reflecting the need for prolonged clinical monitoring, patients in the S25 tier underwent a greater total number of diagnostic PCR tests throughout their hospital courses. Analysis of therapeutic interventions indicated that S25 individuals primarily received medications such as remdesivir or corticosteroids between days 60 and 200, whereas the S50 cohort received treatments predominantly within the first 50 days and the S75 cohort within the initial 30 days. Discover more Get Rapid Tests Read Med Journals Read Health News Find Treatments Find Lung Care Clinical manifestations also diverged markedly between cohorts, as patients with low neutralizing antibody titers suffered protracted illness without acute respiratory collapse. Conversely, individuals in the S50 and S75 groups required immediate pharmaceutical and respiratory intervention and displayed greater vulnerability to acute respiratory distress syndrome during early hospitalization. Underlying comorbidities showed distinct distributions across antibody tiers that may explain divergent immune responses. A substantial proportion of patients in the high-antibody S75 group presented with hypertension, whereas the low-antibody S25 group contained individuals with immunosuppressive conditions such as solid organ transplantation and active chemotherapy, factors that likely attenuated early humoral responses and delayed viral clearance. Testing serum efficacy across viral lineages demonstrated a pronounced reduction in neutralization capacity against newer SARS-CoV-2 variants relative to the ancestral wild-type strain. First-wave patient sera exhibited steep declines in neutralizing activity against BA.1, BA.5, BQ.1.1, XBB, and XBB.1.5, with post-Omicron sera maintaining comparatively higher overall neutralization titers likely resulting from updated vaccinations or hybrid immunity. Comparative binding assays focusing on the XBB sublineage highlighted the biochemical mechanisms driving variant dominance, identifying the solitary S486P amino acid substitution in the receptor-binding domain of XBB.1.5. While neutralization levels against XBB.1 and XBB.1.5 remained comparable in patient sera, optical density measurements confirmed that XBB.1.5 achieved markedly higher binding affinity to the human ACE2 receptor. The authors noted important methodological limitations, emphasizing that the investigation was conducted as a single-center retrospective study with imbalanced cohort sizes across the first wave, Omicron, and post-Omicron periods. Incomplete vaccination and infection records further constrained causal interpretations, leading the research team to call for multi-center longitudinal evaluations to corroborate these immunological and clinical observations. The epidemiological findings contextualize the global impact of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 following its initial identification in Wuhan, China, in December 2019. By December 2024, global records confirmed over 800 million cases and more than 7.1 million deaths worldwide. Although immunization had reached over 70 percent of the global population with at least one vaccine dose by late 2024, contributing to rising seroprevalence and declining daily infections across many regions, emerging variants continue to challenge containment. Waning antibody immunity and the emergence of lineages with greater transmissibility and immune evasion have necessitated booster immunizations alongside ongoing public health surveillance. At the structural level, viral entry into human host cells is mediated by the spike protein, which binds directly to the human angiotensin converting enzyme 2 receptor. Highly mutable regions within this surface protein dictate infection severity and drive immune evasion. Human antibodies directed against receptor-specific epitopes on the spike protein serve as the established correlate of protection against COVID-19 infection. Within the spike protein, the receptor binding domain represents the primary target for neutralizing antibodies. Because neutralizing antibody titers vary widely across individuals, virus neutralization tests established early in the pandemic provide quantitative measurements that offer direct predictive value for evaluating protection against infection. Throughout the pandemic, selective pressures within the spike protein have generated successive variants of concern, including the Alpha, Beta, Gamma, Delta, and Omicron lineages. Emerging subvariants have acquired key mutations that enhance viral fitness and render historical antibody titers progressively ineffective. This evolutionary progression is exemplified by the JN.1 variant, a sublineage derived from BA.2.86 that accumulated notable spike substitutions including L452W and N481K. These mutations conferred heightened transmissibility and immune escape, demonstrating how continuous structural adaptations challenge host defenses and require updated neutralization tests and adapted vaccine compositions to maintain effective population protection. In laboratory evaluations of patient sera across pandemic periods, the authors identified marked differences in neutralization efficacy against specific viral variants. Sera from patients infected during the Omicron wave demonstrated robust neutralizing capacity against the ancestral wild-type strain, with most patient samples exceeding 60 percent neutralization efficacy. However, neutralizing activity against earlier Omicron lineages displayed notable variability. When tested against the BA.1 and BA.5 variants, patient sera exhibited divergent responses, ranging from high neutralization exceeding 90 percent efficacy in certain individuals to an undetectable level of neutralizing activity in others. This observation contrasted with previously published reports from independent cohorts. Although BA.5 possesses specific mutations in the receptor binding domain, namely L452R and F486V, that effectively evade antibodies elicited by vaccination or BA.1 infection, the UCLA cohort showed comparatively lower neutralization against BA.1 than against BA.5. The authors attributed this pattern to cohort demographics and historical public health timelines. In the United States, primary vaccination and booster campaigns occurred extensively throughout 2021, and the lifting of indoor mask mandates in early-to-mid 2022 resulted in widespread community exposure to BA.5, generating elevated antibody titers against that specific variant. Testing across later lineages indicated diminishing neutralization against BQ.1, XBB, and XBB.1.5, reflecting potential immune escape among newly emerging variants. In contrast, serum samples from the post-Omicron cohort consistently retained higher neutralization scores across tested variants compared to first-wave sera. This elevated neutralizing capacity demonstrates substantial improvement in humoral immunity over time, which the researchers linked to the combined immunological benefits of updated vaccination and natural exposure across successive pandemic waves. The investigation also clarified the biochemical mechanisms enabling XBB.1.5 to achieve dominance over its parental variant XBB.1. Genomic analysis identified a solitary amino acid substitution, S486P, in the receptor binding domain of XBB.1.5. Although neutralization titers between XBB.1 and XBB.1.5 were similar, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays revealed distinct receptor binding properties. Comparing optical density at 450 nanometers across log-transformed concentrations demonstrated that XBB.1.5 exhibited steeper sigmoidal curves and higher optical density readings at lower protein concentrations, confirming enhanced binding affinity for the human ACE2 receptor. This indicates that dominant SARS-CoV-2 variants emerge through combined pressures of antibody evasion and increased receptor affinity. Finally, the authors examined how host health conditions influenced antibody production and clinical progression. In the low-antibody S25 cohort, immunosuppressive conditions including organ transplantation and chemotherapy likely blunted initial humoral responses. The researchers suggested these comorbidities attenuated early acute inflammation while delaying viral clearance, explaining why S25 patients experienced protracted hospitalizations and persistent symptoms without severe acute manifestations, ultimately receiving medications between days 60 and 200. In contrast, patients with higher neutralizing antibody levels mounted vigorous early immune responses that triggered acute respiratory distress requiring prompt therapeutic intervention within the initial 30 to 50 days, illustrating how baseline host factors shape clinical trajectories. records.content_title: Ruedas-Gracia, Tiwari Examine Effects of COVID-19 on Belonging
records.content: Nidia Ruedas-Gracia, assistant professor Educational Psychology, and Ananya Tiwari, Ph.D. '23 EPSY, have co-written an article in the Journal of Research on Adolescence that examines the COVID-19 pandemic and it's effects on marginalized girls in India. The study, “Belonging in crisis: A mixed-methods exploration of school disruption among marginalized girls in India,” examines how prolonged COVID-19 school closures reshaped school belonging among marginalized adolescent girls in rural India. Using a bioecological and intersectional lens, it looks at how household labor, digital access, relationships with family, peers, and teachers, and broader gender, caste, and class inequities shaped girls’ connection to school. One key finding is that belonging became increasingly constrained the longer schools stayed closed. "I think it's a great example of the global reach of the work coming out of our doctoral program," says Ruedas-Gracia. "It offers timely lessons about supporting students' sense of belonging when schooling is disrupted." Read the full article here

小 】 时间:2026年11月21日 来源:Cell 45.1 编辑推荐: 理解呼吸道病毒传播需要将病原体基因组数据与详细的流行病学背景相结合。研究人员分析了 2021 年 11 月至 2023 年 1 月在美国马萨诸塞州收集的超过 85,000 例带有流行病学数据的 SARS-CoV-2 基因组(严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒 2,SA 欢迎领取《类器官应用方案 3D之旅》 为了促进科学的传播,生物通采集了这篇文章 订阅BioHot点这里解锁原文链接推送! “畅读会员”点此登录查看原文链接 Article Open access 理解呼吸道病毒传播需要将病原体基因组数据与详细的流行病学背景相结合。研究人员分析了 2021 年 11 月至 2023 年 1 月在美国马萨诸塞州收集的超过 85,000 例带有流行病学数据的 SARS-CoV-2 基因组(严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒 2,SARS-CoV-2)。这些数据来自 666 个场所,包括学校、大学和技术护理机构(skilled nursing facilities,SNFs),使得场所内传播与社区传播风险能够进行直接比较。传播升高集中存在于特定的年龄定义亚群中,包括学校中的高年级青少年、大学中的本科生以及护理机构中的居住者,而其他群体,尤其是工作人员,并未表现出额外风险。年轻成人,特别是大学生,在传播中发挥了不成比例的作用,新的病毒谱系也持续首先在该群体中扩增。病毒扩散呈现出可重复的城市向乡村梯度,疫苗接种与下游传播减少相关。研究人员进一步估计了及时检测新出现变异株所需的测序阈值。总体而言,这些发现揭示了 SARS-CoV-2 传播中一致的人口学和空间结构,可为呼吸道病毒病原体的基因组监测提供依据。 研究背景与意义 欢迎领取《全方位集成的高通量阵列式 SPR 平台》领 取 呼吸道病毒传播的驱动机制不能仅依靠病毒序列变化来解释,还需要把基因组数据与个体年龄、接种状态、居住地、检测场所等流行病学元数据结合起来。此前大规模基因组监测主要服务于新变异株的发现和追踪,虽然能够描绘谱系更替,却往往缺少足够的现场背景,难以回答传播究竟发生在哪些人群、哪些机构环境以及哪些地理通道中。尤其在疫情后期,学校、大学、技术护理机构(skilled nursing facilities,SNFs)和工作场所重新开放或维持运行后,场所内传播是否高于社区背景风险、工作人员是否承担额外风险、年轻成人是否推动新谱系早期扩张,都是公共卫生决策需要证据支持的问题。 这项研究基于马萨诸塞州大范围诊断检测和测序体系,把超过 85,000 例带流行病学元数据的 SARS-CoV-2 基因组与 666 个检测场所联系起来,覆盖 Delta(B.1.1.617.2*)晚期流行以及 BA.1*、BA.2*、BA.4*、BA.5*、BQ.1*、XBB* 等连续 Omicron 亚变体波次。其价值不在于单纯报告变异株比例,而在于用近端遗传相关性(genetic relatedness)作为传播链代理,比较同一场所内病毒基因组是否比同一市镇社区样本更接近,从而识别年龄、场所、城市和接种状态如何共同塑造传播结构。 主要技术方法概括 样本队列来源于 Broad Institute 临床实验室在马萨诸塞州开展的 SARS-CoV-2 诊断检测残余阳性样本,并结合马萨诸塞州公共卫生部及市政卫生部门收集的病例流行病学数据。研究对 134,785 条高质量基因组进行 Pango 谱系注释和 Nextclade 质控,核心分析使用其中 85,125 条带年龄、性别、居住地、接种状态和检测场所元数据的数据。方法上主要采用近端遗传相关性富集分析判断场所内传播是否高于社区背景,利用系统发育树推断州内外输入和市镇间扩散,通过逻辑回归比较不同场所、年龄组和城市类型中新谱系达到 50% 频率的时间差,借助宿主内单核苷酸变异(intrahost single nucleotide variants,iSNVs)识别潜在下游传播,并用二项模型和 PhyloSamp 评估不同每周测序量对新谱系检测时效的影响。 研究结果 超过 85,000 个 SARS-CoV-2 基因组与个体化流行病学数据配对 研究获得 2021 年 11 月 1 日至 2023 年 1 月 17 日期间马萨诸塞州居民的 134,785 条高质量 SARS-CoV-2 基因组,覆盖 492 个 Pango 谱系,并归并为 Delta(B.1.1.617.2*)以及 BA.1*、BA.2*、BA.4*、BA.5*、BQ.1*、XBB* 七个主导谱系。样本来自 666 个机构,分为公共检测、大学、医院诊所、技术护理机构、中小学、其他工作场所和未知部门等七类;其中 85,125 条基因组可链接到去标识化流行病学数据,构成下游分析核心数据集。测序样本总体跟随全州确诊病例趋势,研究期平均每周测序约 10.5% 的确诊病例,为跨场所和跨时间的传播比较提供了高密度基础。 不同人口群体呈现差异化传播模式 研究人员以“同一场所内相距 ≤2 个核苷酸替换且采样间隔 ≤10 天的近缘基因组”相对于同市镇公共检测样本的富集倍数,衡量场所内传播是否超过社区背景。结果显示,技术护理机构近缘基因组富集 4.9 倍(95% CI 4.3–5.5),大学富集 3.3 倍(95% CI 3.1–3.6),中小学仅 1.4 倍(95% CI 1.2–1.7),其他工作场所 1.1 倍(95% CI 0.9–1.3)且不显著。年龄分层进一步表明,风险升高并非机构本身普遍属性,而是集中在特定年龄组:技术护理机构中约 50 岁以后随年龄上升,最高龄者同场所近缘性高出社区约 60 个百分点;学校中主要出现在 15–18 岁,18 岁左右达峰,低龄学生和教职员工接近社区水平;大学中主要集中在 18–22 岁本科生,18–20 岁最强,研究生、教师和工作人员不明显。BA.1*、BA.2*、BA.2.12.1* 在大学达到 50% 频率的时间比其他部门早 4–13 天;排除无症状筛查偏倚后,大学仍最早出现谱系上升,支持年轻成人群体作为早期扩增哨兵人群。 高分辨率时空图谱刻画病毒扩散 研究利用市镇级居住信息和系统发育重建,识别州外输入与州内市镇间移动。新输入显著集中于人口规模大、密度高的城市,城市既是州外输入受体,也是州内扩散源。BA.1* 和 BA.2* 均先在波士顿核心区升高,随后扩散至成熟郊区、区域城市中心、发展中郊区和乡村城镇。遗传距离与地理距离关系显示,≤2 个替换的近缘病毒对主要位于约 15 公里内;当差异累积到 3–5 个替换,即约 4 代传播、约 20 天后,病毒对已可能相隔 100 公里以上;差异超过约 12 个替换时地理结构基本消失,对应约两个月内全州广泛扩散。乡村和发展中郊区同市镇近缘富集达 11.3 倍,高于城市区域的 5.6 倍,说明乡村本地传播链更封闭,而城市承担输入与再分配枢纽角色。 疫苗接种与感染和下传传播减少相关 研究利用 5–11 岁儿童接种推广前后的自然时间点比较发现,学校检测和公共检测中该年龄段病例占比均下降约 50%,Delta 与 BA.1* 均可见。传播层面用两类基因组代理指标评估:一是有无近缘基因组链接,二是宿主内单核苷酸变异(intrahost single nucleotide variants,iSNVs)是否在后继个体共识序列中出现。加强针接种者更常表现为“未链接”,比例为 33.2%,而未加强者为 19.1%;以 iSNVs 判定下游传播时,加强针个体启动至少一次传播的可能性为未接种者的 0.65 倍(0.50–0.84)。仅完成基础免疫而未加强者与未接种者差异不显著。Ct 值分析显示接种剂次增加与较低病毒载量相关,距末次接种时间延长与病毒载量轻度回升相关,但行为混杂不能被排除。 测序强度决定新谱系检测速度 基于全部 130,000 条基因组进行降采样模拟,研究发现每周测序 100 条基因组时,多数谱系能在其达到 1% 流行率前被检出;每周 50 条通常只延迟数天;检测概率随测序量上升到每周约 500 条后趋于平台期。BA.1* 因增长过快,提高测序量对提前发现帮助有限。若目标是识别“正在指数增长的新谱系”,从 3% 频率后开始拟合逻辑增长,每周 300 条可在 14 天内确认 BA.1* 类快速上升谱系;对 BA.5* 这类慢增长谱系,14 天内确认几乎不可达到,21 天内确认至少需每周 400 条。 讨论与研究结论翻译 讨论部分指出,在学校、大学和技术护理机构中,SARS-CoV-2 传播升高主要不是机构环境的普遍效应,而是由特定年龄亚群驱动;工作人员、低龄学生以及多数其他工作场所并未显示明显高于社区的传播风险。技术护理机构是唯一呈现稳定场所内传播富集的场景,风险主要指向老年居住者;学校和大学的风险集中在 15–18 岁及 18–22 岁,可能与该年龄段的社交网络和住宿模式有关。18–22 岁人群,尤其大学生,是新谱系早期扩增的前哨群体。空间上,新谱系优先经大城市输入,再向郊区、区域城市和乡村扩散,约两个月完成全州铺开;因此城市应侧重阻断输入,乡村应侧重切断本地传播链。测序监测方面,中等且持续的覆盖率已能获得大部分早期预警收益,过高测序量的边际增益有限。作者同时强调,数据来自机会性监测,缺少未感染者接种信息和个体行为数据,不能做因果推断。 研究结论部分可译为:大规模基因组监测加深了对 COVID-19 大流行期间 SARS-CoV-2 变异株出现与扩散的认识,但缺乏详细元数据常限制更深入的流行病学分析。本研究利用跨多个变异株波次、高分辨率、并与流行病学元数据链接的大规模 SARS-CoV-2 基因组监测数据,考察了病毒传播的时空格局、不同人口群体和场所之间传播动力学的差异,以及与感染和下游传播相关的因素;同时给出了及时检测已知关注变异株、识别频率上升的未知变异株所需测序率的实用估计。尽管数据来自快速演变公共卫生应急中的机会式基因组监测,本研究仍展示了整合基因组与流行病学信息以解析精细尺度传播格局的能力。通过识别最可能在场所内外驱动传播的人群,以及新变异株最可能被检测到的时点,研究结果为未来基因组监测系统设计提供了可操作依据,尤其支持对高传播人群进行定向采样。 records.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Monday, November 23, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Biology SARS-CoV-2 Beta Variant Drives Acute Lung Immune Activation in Wild-Type Mice by November 20, 2026 in Biology Reading Time: 6 mins read 0 SARS-CoV-2 Beta Variant Drives Acute Lung Immune Activation in Wild-Type Mice Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram Researchers investigating pulmonary immune dynamics during coronavirus infections have completed a whole-transcriptomic evaluation of lung tissues from wild-type mice exposed to a clinical isolate of the SARS-CoV-2 Beta variant. While ancestral lineages of SARS-CoV-2 failed to infect standard laboratory rodents because the viral spike protein did not recognize murine Ace2 receptors, specific mutations within the Beta variant (lineage B.1.351) permit productive viral replication in non-transgenic animals. This experimental investigation demonstrates that wild-type C57BL/6J mice mount an intense, early inflammatory and transcriptomic response upon intranasal challenge with the Beta variant, presenting an accessible physiological system for probing virus-induced lung injury without the confounding fatal encephalitis characteristic of transgenic models expressing human ACE2. To establish the molecular consequences of infection in non-modified animals, investigators administered intranasal inoculations of either phosphate-buffered saline as a vehicle control or ten thousand plaque-forming units of the clinical SARS-CoV-2 B.1.351 strain to six-week-old male and female C57BL/6J mice. The experimental cohort was housed under approved animal biosafety level 3 containment protocols, ensuring strict environmental isolation during active viral exposure. Following exposure, primary lung tissues were harvested at defined temporal intervals of three and six days post-infection after systemic perfusion with cold phosphate-buffered saline. Total ribonucleic acid was extracted from homogenized tissue specimens to verify viral persistence and evaluate shifting transcriptional patterns across the acute phase of host immune engagement. Quantitative reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction targeting the viral nucleocapsid gene confirmed active replication within pulmonary tissues at both harvested intervals. Viral transcript copies were detectable at elevated levels at day three post-infection but demonstrated a statistically significant reduction by day six. This rapid reduction in detectable viral genome copies indicates that wild-type host defense mechanisms successfully engaged the pathogen to suppress continuing replication within the respiratory compartment. The clearance trajectory observed across these time points provided an essential biological framework for contextualizing the parallel shifts in global host gene regulation, allowing researchers to evaluate how transcriptional activity correlates with viral clearance. High-throughput messenger RNA sequencing conducted on ten independent complementary DNA libraries revealed marked differences in global gene expression between uninfected controls and virus-exposed groups. Bioinformatic filtering using the Limma-Voom analytical framework established differential expression thresholds at an absolute log2 fold change exceeding 0.75 coupled with a Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted significance value below 0.05. At day three post-infection, the computational pipeline resolved 285 differentially expressed genes comprising 273 significantly upregulated targets and 12 downregulated transcripts. By day six post-infection, the total number of dysregulated genes dropped sharply to 46 transcripts, which included 43 upregulated and 3 downregulated genes, reflecting the parallel reduction in lung viral burden. An evaluation of temporal patterns demonstrated that day three post-infection was dominated by early innate defense mechanisms and potent antiviral pathways. Variance-filtered heatmaps identified intense early activation of interferon-stimulated transcripts, including Mx1, Irf7, Oas1a, Oas1g, Oas2, Oas3, Ifi204, Ifi205, and Ifi211. In parallel, chemokine signaling transcripts such as Ccl2 and Ccl7, alongside regulatory markers linked to host cell progression including Zbp1, Pbk, Rad51, and Esco2, exhibited pronounced transcript increases. These robust molecular responses illustrate how the unprimed pulmonary epithelium and resident immune populations rapidly mobilize transcription factors and downstream defense mediators immediately following entry of the Beta variant. By day six post-infection, the pulmonary transcriptomic profile shifted toward secondary immune-mediated tissue turnover and structural modification. Canonical pathway enrichment demonstrated changes in genes participating in oxidative phosphorylation, calcium signaling, and cellular turnover, highlighted by altered expression of Gzmb, Pbcd1, Cdca2, and Top2a. Gene Ontology functional mapping underscored substantial alterations in structural transcripts associated with the extracellular matrix, myofibril assemblies, and sarcomeres, accompanied by modifications in hydrolase and oxidoreductase enzyme activity. These observations align with tissue-level processes wherein early antiviral cytokine cascades transition into subsequent cellular clearance, tissue remodeling, and apoptotic resolution. Targeted pathway-level analyses further detailed the coordinated activation of inflammatory and programmed cell death circuits across both observational intervals. Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes mapping revealed early enrichment of pathways governing endocytosis, cellular senescence, tumor necrosis factor signaling, nuclear factor kappa B activation, and NOD-like receptor cascades at day three. Notably, transcripts associated with programmed cell death mechanisms, such as apoptosis and pyroptosis, did not undergo uniform simultaneous upregulation. Instead, they exhibited a staggered activation profile where specific mediators like Daxx, FasL, and Gzmb demonstrated divergent temporal dynamics between days three and six, while complement and coagulation factors including Fga, Serpina1c, and C6 displayed amplified induction at the later sampling point. Comparative network evaluations revealed a core group of 43 differentially expressed genes that remained consistently dysregulated across both post-infection sampling dates. Protein-protein interaction networks constructed via Cytoscape identified three distinct functional interaction clusters through the MCODE algorithm. Utilizing the maximal clique centrality metric within the CytoHubba application, investigators established the top ten hub genes coordinating these persistent networks: Prc1, Ube2c, Ccnb2, Ncapg, Aurkb, Cep55, Mki67, Dlgap5, Ccna2, and Kif11. These hub transcripts primarily direct fundamental mitotic processes, including chromosome segregation, spindle assembly, and DNA replication, indicating that viral challenge directly impacts pulmonary cell cycle architecture. To validate sequencing determinations through independent biochemical assays, researchers conducted targeted quantitative real-time PCR alongside multiplex bead-based protein immunoassays. Relative gene expression assays confirmed elevated transcript copies of inflammatory markers Tnfa, Il6, Ccl2, and Ccl3, showing significantly greater fold changes on day three than on day six. Multiplex protein quantification of lung homogenates corroborated these findings, demonstrating statistically significant elevations in interleukin-6, CCL2, CXCL2, CXCL10, G-CSF, and GM-CSF at day three post-infection, alongside sustained elevations in TNF-alpha, IL-5, and IL-12 at both intervals, while anti-inflammatory cytokine IL-4 levels dropped significantly. Collectively, these transcriptomic and proteomic findings confirm that the clinical SARS-CoV-2 Beta variant drives a genuine, self-resolving inflammatory pulmonary challenge in wild-type mice without artificial transgene modification. While transgenic rodent models expressing human ACE2 frequently succumb to severe neurotropic pathology absent in typical human clinical presentations, wild-type C57BL/6J animals maintain localized respiratory viral replication and pronounced immune activation. By cataloging the distinct molecular signatures, functional hub networks, and cytokine cascades induced by this clinical variant, the investigation establishes a robust baseline for studying pulmonary immune defenses and evaluating targeted therapeutic strategies in standard experimental rodents. The global public health context surrounding SARS-CoV-2 evolution underscores the importance of evaluating non-adapted variant transmission in standard animal hosts. Since December 2019, SARS-CoV-2 has driven approximately 641 million documented infections and contributed to more than 6.6 million deaths worldwide. Although the ancestral virus demonstrated minimal phenotypic alteration in the early phases of the pandemic, emerging lineages designated as variants of concern, such as the Beta variant first recognized after October 2020, accumulated critical structural modifications. The B.1.351 lineage possesses eight distinct amino acid variations within its spike protein that directly alter the binding affinity of the receptor-binding domain. These changes not only enhance the strength of viral attachment to host entry receptors and diminish neutralization by antibodies elicited by approved vaccines, but also enable the pathogen to engage native murine Ace2, overcoming the species-specific barrier that spared standard rodents during ancestral outbreaks. Technical assessment of sequencing reliability provided crucial verification for the pulmonary transcriptomic catalog. Analysis of ten constructed complementary DNA libraries demonstrated high raw and clean throughput exceeding 40 million paired reads per specimen, accompanied by stable guanine-cytosine percentages ranging between 47 and 50 percent. Quality metrics across sequencing runs remained high, with more than 93 percent of sequenced bases satisfying the Q20 benchmark and greater than 92 percent surpassing the rigorous Q30 threshold. High-molecular integrity was verified prior to library construction via capillary electrophoresis, ensuring RNA integrity numbers exceeded 7.0 across harvested lung samples. Mapping aligned cDNA fragments against the mm10 mouse reference genome via StringTie enabled precise measurement of normalized fragments per kilobase of transcript per million mapped reads, establishing a dependable baseline for subsequent differential gene expression modeling. Bioinformatic comparisons between this model and published human clinical data further clarify how murine pulmonary responses mirror broader disease pathology. Several hub genes identified within the persistent interaction network, notably Prc1 and Ccnb2, show dysregulated expression patterns shared with patients suffering from severe human COVID-19 as well as chronic pulmonary disorders such as silicosis. Complementary transcriptomic surveys have likewise highlighted Ube2c, Kif11, and Aurkb as critical targets altered during severe human viral illness across pulmonary, systemic immune, and reproductive tissues. Marked modulation of the proliferation marker Mki67 confirms that the Beta variant disrupts regular cell cycle progression in infected lung tissue. Moreover, comparative pathway analyses align with findings from cultured human lung epithelial cells, where viral challenge triggers coordinated interferon cascades, broad cytokine induction, and pronounced cellular regulatory shifts. Despite these findings, essential methodological boundaries constrain direct extrapolation to clinical human therapy. Experimental groups comprised small cohort sizes of three to four animals per experimental condition, which may limit statistical resolution for subtle regulatory shifts, as evidenced by modest non-significant elevations of interleukin-6, CCL2, and CXCL2 protein levels measured at day six post-infection. Furthermore, the overall severity of pulmonary pathology observed in these non-modified rodents remained distinctly lower than the severe disease courses documented in transgenic models overexpressing human ACE2 receptors. Investigators did not assess extended longitudinal outcomes beyond the six-day observation window, leaving long-term tissue remodeling and prolonged viral clearance unanswered within this initial transcriptomic framework. Investigating the lingering outcomes among survivors of the initial wave, researchers collected survey data to determine symptom prevalence and evaluate demographic, clinical, and environmental variables linked to post-infection health conditions. In a sample comprising 47,464 participants from the general population, researchers found an overall long COVID prevalence of 52.34 percent, observing a gradual decline in reported conditions between the successive assessment periods. The study design relied on two distinct survey waves administered online in August 2023 and August 2024 to systematically capture participant health profiles and persistent symptoms. Through these structured assessments, investigators gathered detailed records covering medical history, psychological health, everyday nutritional habits, community settings, and vaccination records. Across the evaluated clinical manifestations, fatigue emerged as the most prevalent lingering symptom reported by individuals following their acute COVID-19 infections, standing out among the sequelae monitored across the surveyed regions of mainland China. Discover more Find Treatments Donate to Research Track Outbreaks To pinpoint variables associated with persistent symptoms, the researchers performed both univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses, presenting all associations as odds ratios accompanied by 95 percent confidence intervals. The statistical evaluations revealed that specific demographic and pre-existing medical conditions were positively associated with increased odds of long COVID. Female participants had higher odds of lingering symptoms compared to males, exhibiting an odds ratio of 1.17 with a 95 percent confidence interval from 1.12 to 1.22. Additionally, individuals aged 18 to 59 years showed higher odds of reporting prolonged symptoms, yielding an odds ratio of 1.21 with a confidence interval ranging from 1.11 to 1.32. Discover more Get Rapid Tests Read Med Journals Read Health News View Census Data Pre-existing physical and psychological morbidities displayed particularly pronounced positive associations with long COVID among the surveyed individuals. Participants diagnosed with any chronic diseases had more than double the odds of experiencing protracted sequelae, recording an odds ratio of 2.19 and a 95 percent confidence interval between 2.07 and 2.31. The presence of mental disorders was associated with nearly triple the odds of lingering symptoms, marked by an odds ratio of 2.98 with a confidence interval spanning 2.85 to 3.11. Behavioral factors also contributed to these associations, with alcohol drinking showing a positive correlation to persistent symptoms at an odds ratio of 1.23 and a confidence interval of 1.17 to 1.29. Conversely, the regression models identified multiple lifestyle and dietary habits that demonstrated significant inverse associations with long COVID. Participants maintaining a regular sleep-wake schedule exhibited lower odds of ongoing symptoms, reflecting an odds ratio of 0.81 with a 95 percent confidence interval of 0.77 to 0.84. Nutritional factors also showed inverse associations; combining meat and vegetable diets yielded an odds ratio of 0.83, while daily vegetable intake alone similarly displayed an odds ratio of 0.83. Daily consumption of animal foods and daily dairy products were also inversely associated with long COVID, recording odds ratios of 0.91 with confidence intervals of 0.86 to 0.96 and 0.85 to 0.98, respectively, alongside daily sunbathing of at least five hours, which registered an odds ratio of 0.93. Social and physical living environments were also inversely linked to long COVID occurrence within the analyzed cohorts. Individuals reporting a satisfactory relationship with their neighbors had lower odds of persistent symptoms, showing an odds ratio of 0.81 with a confidence interval between 0.75 and 0.87. A satisfactory community environment exhibited a stronger inverse association, marked by an odds ratio of 0.71 and a confidence interval ranging from 0.66 to 0.75. Furthermore, vaccination demonstrated a consistent protective association against long COVID across multiple dose thresholds, with odds ratios of 0.85 for two doses, 0.87 for three doses, and 0.81 for four or more doses compared to unstratified baseline references. The authors concluded that long COVID continues to represent a major public health challenge influenced by a broad matrix of individual, behavioral, and environmental elements. They noted that targeted monitoring, early identification, and proactive management of at-risk groups could offer substantial value for health systems. Proposed strategies highlighted in the findings include community-level programs focusing on balanced nutrition and sleep hygiene alongside sustained immunization efforts. The investigators also emphasized the potential policy benefits of establishing a national surveillance framework and integrating screening protocols into routine primary care to support high-risk populations. These findings, derived from the national framework for influenza-like illness (ILI) and severe acute respiratory infection (SARI), underscore the current epidemiological burden of these pathogens in the region. The study, which utilized RT-PCR testing on respiratory specimens, found an nearly equal distribution between SARI and ILI cases, representing 50.1% and 49.9% of the total cohort, respectively. The majority of individuals seeking care fell within the 16 to 50 age group, accounting for 55.9% of the study population. Through logistic regression analysis, the research team identified age as a significant factor in patient outcomes; specifically, increasing age, alongside pre-existing conditions such as diabetes mellitus, heart disease, chronic respiratory diseases, and chronic hematological diseases, were identified as independent predictors of SARI. Discover more Find Lung Care Read Med Journals Find Treatments Influenza positivity rates showed distinct demographic variations, with the highest prevalence observed among patients aged 6 to 15 years and those with underlying medical comorbidities. While increasing age was independently associated with lower odds of testing positive for influenza, patients suffering from chronic conditions including diabetes, heart disease, respiratory issues, and kidney disease faced significantly higher odds of a positive influenza test. Discover more Get Cold Relief Track Outbreaks Check Symptoms Get Rapid Tests Regarding viral circulation, influenza A predominated during the study period, with dominance alternating between the A/H1N1pdm09 and A/H3N2 subtypes. Notably, all identified influenza B cases were classified as belonging to the Victoria lineage, with no evidence found for the circulation of the Yamagata lineage. The recurring winter seasonal pattern for influenza activity emphasizes the critical need for regional health officials to prioritize vaccination campaigns before the peak season begins. The study concludes that enhancing national sentinel surveillance systems and laboratory testing capacity is essential for more accurate detection and ongoing management. By identifying circulating strains and understanding the epidemiological risks posed by specific comorbidities, health authorities can better guide future vaccination strategies and bolster overall public health preparedness against respiratory threats in Iraq. Researchers investigated how epidemiologically emerging viral strains interact with human peripheral blood mononuclear cells, tracing changes across antiviral, inflammatory, and antigen-presenting functions using high-dimensional immunophenotyping, secretome profiling, and functional assays. The investigation utilized a human peripheral blood mononuclear cell in vitro model to assess cellular reprogramming across multiple viral lineages. Investigators exposed primary immune cells to the ancestral D614G strain, alongside the Alpha, Beta, Gamma, Delta, Omicron BA.1, and recombinant Omicron XBB.1 variants, systematically comparing the immune signaling and cellular remodeling triggered by each lineage. Single-cell multi-omic profiling following exposure to Omicron BA.1 revealed substantial remodeling across the innate immune compartment. The analysis identified a particularly marked dampening of monocyte differentiation and functional maturation, establishing circulating monocytes as primary targets for innate immune alteration following viral challenge. Direct tracking of viral components confirmed that the virus preferentially accumulated within monocytes. By conducting viral RNA mapping and detecting double-stranded RNA-positive cells, the study authors observed localized accumulation of viral material that directly coincided with transcriptomic reprogramming inside the monocyte population. Analysis of cytokine and chemokine production indicated that the emergence of Omicron altered the inflammatory baseline compared to earlier lineages. Omicron exposure produced a more balanced inflammatory profile characterized by preserved antiviral type I interferon responses and moderated chemokine induction, pointing toward a regulated virus-host equilibrium. The study demonstrated that this shifted equilibrium was associated with reduced innate immune-mediated tissue damage in vitro. While earlier lineages triggered distinct inflammatory patterns, the moderation of chemokine induction under Omicron exposure indicated variant-specific calibration of early host immune responses. In contrast to BA.1, the post-Omicron recombinant subvariant XBB.1 robustly re-engaged host antiviral pathways. Cellular stimulation with XBB.1 induced high type I interferon release and uniquely promoted interleukin-12p70 production, highlighting divergence among closely related Omicron sublineages. The induction of interleukin-12p70 by XBB.1 drove the expansion of specific dendritic cell populations, including antiviral, mature PD-L1-positive CD80-positive plasmacytoid dendritic cells and BDCA3-positive conventional dendritic cells. These expanded dendritic cell subsets directly supported the priming of CD8-positive T cells. The authors concluded that circulating variants possess intrinsic differences that govern monocyte targeting, inflammation, and antigen presentation. These observations provide a detailed laboratory framework for evaluating how progressive viral mutations influence innate immune defense and subsequent cellular interactions in vitro. Sign up here HomeNewsNew Covid-19 variant is already circulating in Europe New Covid-19 variant is already circulating in Europe A new variant of the SARS-CoV-2 virus (PJ.2.1) is currently circulating on several continents and has already been detected in Europe. By Íris Marçal, in News · 19 Nov 2026 · 1 Comments Credits: Unsplash; Author: Fusion Medical Animation; It has features which may lead to increased transmissibility and faster spread of the disease. First identified in Canada in May 2026, the variant has since been detected in Spain, France, the Netherlands, the US, Brazil, Israel, Australia and New Zealand. As reported in a data release by the journal News Medical Life Sciences, the key difference in the PJ.2.1 variant is in the spike protein, which has a higher affinity for binding to the receptors on the surface of human cells, thus enabling more efficient infection. In all other clinical terms, the variant is very much like the other sublineages that the public has seen; there is no evidence to suggest it is any more or less severe in terms of the illness it causes. The classic symptom profile remains the same: fever, cough, sore throat, nasal congestion/runny nose, headaches, myalgia, fatigue and changes to the sense of taste and smell. Despite the increased transmissibility of this variant, the current booster vaccines are still effective at neutralising the virus according to the research. As per the research cited by News Medical Life Sciences, "the results suggest that vaccination does protect against the PJ.2.1 variant. The situation could, of course, change if the variant acquires further mutations which would enable it to escape the immune response." In Portugal, the seasonal COVID-19 immunisation campaign has now seen over 884,000 people immunised between 30 September and 15 November 2026. The importance of this monitoring is underlined by the latest WHO data, which shows 719 deaths in 31 countries between 21 September and 18 October, an increase on the 542 deaths in the previous 28 days, with seven countries in Europe and the Americas seeing a rise in mortality of over 10% and the majority of those deaths being in the 65+ age group. records.content_title: Development of Explosive Acne Fulminans After SARS-CoV-2 Vaccine Administration: A Case Report
records.content: Abstract This is a case study of a 23-year-old, active-duty male with a history of acne vulgaris but no personal history of vaccination reactions who was administered the severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) vaccine and subsequently developed nodulocystic acne. He denied excessive physical activity, current anabolic steroid use, and changes in medications during that time frame; however, he admitted to using anabolic steroids and testosterone in the year prior to vaccine administration. The patient had dozens of thick, firm hypertrophic pink scars on the chest and back with surrounding tan macules on his back. The patient was treated with oral isotretinoin and pulsed dye laser (PDL) with eventual post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation noted after treatment. Although acne fulminans (AF) developed one month after SARS-CoV-2 administration, this is a hypothesis-generating clinical observation and temporal proximity alone does not prove causation. Introduction Acne maligna or acne fulminans (AF) is a rare dermatologic disorder that often presents acutely as a painful, ulcerative, and hemorrhagic form of acne [1]. According to Bhatia et al. (2021), there have been fewer than 200 reported cases of AF, most of which involve young men with various clinical presentations [2]. In certain patients, it may be associated with more systemic symptoms, including polyarthritis and fever [1]. In addition, AF may lead to bone lesions and laboratory abnormalities [1]. Because of its rarity, the etiology of AF is not well understood. Massa et al. (2017) describe the use of high-dose isotretinoin as a potential trigger of AF when treating patients with severe acne. They also describe the role of Propionibacterium acnes in activating the inflammatory cascade seen in the development of acne, often universally [3]. In addition, an association with synovitis-acne-pustulosis-hyperostosis-osteitis (SAPHO) syndrome and the response to infliximab highlight that increased levels of inflammatory cytokines, most notably tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), may play a role in AF pathogenesis [4]. Lastly, Saint-Jean et al. (2015) suggest that testosterone use and disuse may also trigger AF [5]. In fact, Melnik et al. (2007) documented a case of AF in a bodybuilder who was self-medicating with anabolic steroids and testosterone [6]. This observational study demonstrated AF development after severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) administration, but temporal proximity alone does not prove causation, and causality cannot be established. Case Presentation Our patient was a 23-year-old, active-duty male with a history of acne vulgaris and no personal history of vaccination reactions who was administered the SARS-CoV-2 vaccine and subsequently developed nodulocystic acne. The patient was administered the Pfizer SARS-CoV-2 vaccine in mid-January 2022. In Month 1, the patient presented to Dermatology with symptoms of painful and tender ulcerated nodules on the chest and back, bilateral shoulder pain, mild fatigue, but denied sudden or fluctuating fever and weight loss resulting in extreme malaise. The patient denied excessive physical activity, current anabolic steroid use, and changes in medications during that time frame; however, he admitted to using anabolic steroids and testosterone in the year prior to vaccine administration. He denied allergies altogether, including drug, environmental, and food. His personal vaccination history included meningococcal vaccine (MGC), Adenovirus, polio, tetanus, diphtheria (Td), Hepatitis A, and annual influenza vaccination. Vitals demonstrated a minimally elevated temperature of 99.8 °F, but were otherwise unremarkable. Physical exam was significant for (1) open and closed comedones, (2) inflammatory papules and pustules, (3) nodular lesions, and (4) severe acneiform scarring on chest and back, including linear stria-like scarring on shoulders (Figure 1). Labs taken in mid-February 2022 did not demonstrate leukocytosis or elevated inflammatory markers, CRP, and ESR at the time (Table 1). An allergy and immune workup, outside of CRP and ESR, was not performed, leaving alternative triggers unresolved. AF is diagnosed clinically by the abrupt onset of severe inflammatory acne characterized by painful, ulcerative, and hemorrhagic nodules and pustules, typically involving the upper trunk. Systemic manifestations may include fever, malaise, myalgia, and arthralgia. Laboratory findings may include leukocytosis and elevated inflammatory markers; however, no specific laboratory abnormality is diagnostic. Other diagnoses considered were acne conglobata and rosacea fulminans. Based on the sudden, explosive onset and visual examination coupled with subjective systemic symptoms, the patient was diagnosed with AF. The patient was prescribed Accutane 10 mg daily along with 1 mg/kg/day oral prednisolone. He presented for follow-up in Month 2, with remission of systemic symptoms and improvement of nodular lesions and papules but continued hypertrophic scarring. Accutane was increased to 40 mg daily and oral prednisolone was discontinued. During follow-up in Month 4, the patient continued to have multiple nodular lesions and papules, and Accutane was increased to 80 mg daily. He presented to follow-up in Month 6 with improved response and few nodules and papules compared to treatment onset (Figure 2). Although the patient did have significant hypertrophic scarring on the shoulders, back, and chest, which was treated with intralesional triamcinolone and pulsed dye laser (PDL) with a positive response. The patient has since transferred to a different command. Discussion As a result of SARS-CoV-2 mass vaccination, there have been increased reports of cutaneous adverse events (CAEs) that have been related to the administration of the SARS-CoV-2 vaccine [7]. McMahon et al. (2021) conducted a registry-based retrospective study that documented cutaneous reactions following messenger RNA (mRNA)-1273 (Moderna) and BNT162b2 (Pfizer-BioNTech) COVID-19 vaccinations in 414 subjects [8]. Although a spectrum of CAEs were recorded, the most common reactions were local injection site reactions, erythromelalgia, flares of psoriasis, and swelling [8]. Kim et al. (2023) documented a rare case of AF in a 15-year-old male after COVID-19 vaccination administration [9]. This CAE was in the absence of new drug administration, signs of infection, or immunological factors known to trigger AF [9]. Despite the absence of some alternative precipitating factors, causality remains unproven given the lack of epidemiologic evidence, the single-case design, and the inability to consider all confounding factors. Bhargava et al. (2022) describe a separate report of a neutrophilic pustular eruption five days after ChAdOx1 nCoV-19 vaccination [10]. Despite initially having AF in their differential, Bhargava et al. favored a Behcet-like inflammatory eruption due to the acral distribution and prominent genital and oral ulcerations uncharacteristic of AF [10]. Regardless, the limited direct evidence in the case, coupled with AF not being the diagnosis, further disputes a causal association between vaccine administration and AF. Collectively, the available literature provides limited cases of documented AF after COVID-19 vaccination. Due to the rarity of reported cases, the possibility of alternative confounding factors, and the lack of controlled studies, causal certainty cannot be established. Conclusions This patient was an otherwise healthy, 23-year-old, active-duty male with a history of acne vulgaris but not AF, with no recent medication changes, changes in physical or dietary regimens, or relevant family history. Although admitting to prior anabolic steroid and testosterone use in the past, he denies usage during the year prior to vaccine administration. There were limitations with this observational study, which did not address all alternative triggers such as hormonal imbalances, known genetic predisposition, and viral infections associated with SAPHO syndrome. The study also took place in the setting of temporal coincidence and absence of causal evidence. The association with SARS-CoV-2 vaccine administration and AF development is preliminary, unproven, and hypothesis-generating, and more research needs to be done to better inform future patients who may be at risk. By systematically comparing wastewater consensus genomes with clinical sequencing data from the same urban catchment, researchers established that environmental monitoring can capture viral genomic diversity that is often underrepresented in patient-derived samples. This work, conducted under the Indian SARS-CoV-2 Genomics Consortium (INSACOG), highlights the capacity of wastewater-based epidemiology to function as an early-warning framework for emerging viral lineages and persistent mutation patterns. The findings provide a detailed evaluation of how environmental genomic surveillance can complement conventional clinical testing, particularly in densely populated urban environments where clinical sequencing may be constrained by diagnostic access or asymptomatic infection dynamics. Between March 2023 and January 2024, the research team collected approximately 1-liter grab samples of untreated influent wastewater twice weekly from ten major sewage treatment plants (STPs) in Surat. This high-frequency sampling effort resulted in 945 collected samples, which were subsequently processed to identify SARS-CoV-2 viral RNA. Of the 945 samples, 368 tested positive for SARS-CoV-2, representing a 38.9% positivity rate. To ensure high-quality genomic data, samples with a cycle threshold (Ct) value below 30 were selected for whole-genome sequencing, resulting in the successful assembly of 51 high-quality wastewater consensus genomes. This dataset was then analyzed alongside a comprehensive clinical dataset comprising 1,814 SARS-CoV-2 genomes collected from the same region between March 2020 and January 2025. By aligning these two distinct data streams, the investigators aimed to quantify mutation concordance, calculate temporal lead times for variant detection, and identify recurrent genomic signatures. Discover more genomic Genomics Get Rapid Tests The comparative analysis revealed substantial insight into the distinct but complementary nature of the two surveillance methods. The environmental dataset was primarily dominated by clades 23B and 24A, whereas the clinical cohort showed a higher prevalence of older lineages, specifically clades 21J and 21K. The study identified 953 mutations shared between the wastewater and clinical datasets, accounting for the majority of the variation observed in the environmental genomes. However, the analysis also uncovered 205 mutations that were exclusively detected in wastewater and absent from the selected clinical dataset. These exclusive variants highlight the potential of wastewater-based epidemiology to capture under-sampled transmission chains, asymptomatic infections, or prolonged shedding events that might otherwise remain hidden from clinical diagnostic networks. The distribution of these mutations varied across the viral genome, with higher sharing proportions observed in the structural Envelope, Membrane, and Spike genes, compared to the accessory or non-structural regions. Discover more Study Biology Genomic genomics Order DNA Kits A critical outcome of the study was the identification of specific mutation signals that appeared in the wastewater months prior to their documentation in clinical sequencing. Fifteen distinct mutations were detected in wastewater before their first observation in the clinical sequence dataset, with lead times ranging from 21 to 187 days. Notably, the spike protein mutation S:I670V was detected in wastewater 187 days before appearing in any clinical genome from the region. Similarly, the ORF1a:F499L mutation was detected 145 days earlier in the environmental samples. These temporal differences suggest that wastewater can act as a leading indicator of emerging mutation profiles, provided that the clinical sequencing intensity remains below the threshold required to capture these low-frequency variants in individual patient samples. While these lead times are influenced by the intensity of regional clinical sequencing, they provide empirical evidence of the value of integrated surveillance strategies. The longitudinal data also facilitated the identification of nine mutations that remained detectable in wastewater for approximately 147 days, from August 2023 to January 2024. These recurrently co-detected mutations—including ORF1a:F536V, ORF1a:A211D, ORF1a:N2526S, ORF1a:V3593F, S:V127F, S:E554K, S:A570V, S:P621S, and M:T30A—were repeatedly observed across 15 to 16 independent wastewater genomes. Because consensus sequences from mixed environmental samples cannot confirm that multiple mutations occur on the same viral genome, the authors note that these patterns do not necessarily represent a single coordinated haplotype or a novel variant. However, their prolonged, recurrent co-detection indicates a sustained presence of related viral populations within the catchment, warranting further investigation into whether these signatures reflect ongoing transmission or specific shedding dynamics that clinical networks fail to capture. Lineage dynamics within the wastewater network further demonstrated the utility of the approach in tracking evolutionary shifts. Throughout the surveillance period, the catchment showed a transition in dominance from XBB.1.16 in the early months of 2023 to the JN.1.1.6 sublineage by January 2024. This longitudinal tracking of lineage replacement provided a clear picture of circulating variants within the sewer catchment, capturing shifts in viral composition without relying on hospital-based diagnostic sampling. The study highlights that by integrating viral contributions from broad population segments, environmental surveillance effectively mitigates the biases introduced by differential healthcare-seeking behavior, population density, and clinical testing availability, offering a more representative snapshot of community-level viral circulation than clinical genomes alone. Despite these significant observations, the study identifies several methodological limitations, primarily related to the asymmetry between the two compared datasets. The clinical dataset was approximately 35 times larger than the wastewater dataset and spanned a significantly longer period. Consequently, while the detection of wastewater-exclusive mutations is a promising indicator of the method’s sensitivity, it cannot be definitively categorized as proof of early transmission without further verification through read-level analysis or haplotype-deconvolution. Additionally, the study relies on consensus-based variant calling, which is inherently limited in its ability to resolve low-frequency minority variants in complex wastewater mixtures. These technical challenges emphasize that environmental surveillance should be interpreted as a complementary asset to, rather than a replacement for, conventional clinical surveillance. The interpretation of the observed differences in clade distribution and exclusive mutation detection must also account for technical factors. Variations in sequencing depth, amplicon coverage, and consensus-calling thresholds between pooled wastewater samples and individual clinical specimens can generate apparent differences in variant detection. The authors caution that clinical co-occurrence should not be assumed to validate every wastewater variant call, and that the observed discrepancies may reflect these technical nuances alongside genuine biological differences in the populations being sampled. The study explicitly distinguishes between these technical explanations and the intended public health application of the data, reinforcing the importance of rigorous bioinformatic pipelines to minimize consensus-calling artifacts. To address these computational challenges, the researchers developed and utilized an automated, open-source bioinformatics pipeline specifically designed for cryptic variant detection and longitudinal environmental surveillance. This tool streamlines the complexities of variant calling, functional annotation, and mutation co-occurrence assessment, effectively lowering the barriers to rigorous and reproducible environmental genomics. By making this workflow available to the broader scientific community, the study provides a scalable model that is readily adaptable for monitoring other infectious agents, antimicrobial resistance markers, and metagenomic samples. The deployment of standardized, automated tools is presented as an essential step in transforming environmental genomics from a specialized research activity into a routine public health asset. From a One Health perspective, the study highlights how the integration of environmental and clinical data provides a more comprehensive understanding of pathogen circulation, transmission dynamics, and evolutionary change than either system can achieve independently. While clinical surveillance remains indispensable for characterizing patient-level outcomes, environmental genomic surveillance offers a practical mechanism for detecting emerging threats at the population scale. The ability to monitor persistent genomic signatures and identify mutation signals in advance of clinical surges is particularly valuable for preparing for future infectious disease threats. The research team concludes that building resilient public health infrastructures requires such integrated surveillance networks to translate raw sequence data into actionable, near-real-time intelligence for disease preparedness and proactive response. records.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Monday, November 23, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Urban Rodents in Brazzaville Healthcare Facilities Harbor SARS-CoV-2 Infection and Antibodies by November 17, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 6 mins read 0 Urban Rodents in Brazzaville Healthcare Facilities Harbor SARS-CoV-2 Infection and Antibodies Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram Researchers investigating urban wildlife in the Republic of the Congo have documented the presence of SARS-CoV-2 infection and exposure among wild rodents living within healthcare facilities in the capital city of Brazzaville. Conducted between April 13 and December 30, 2022, the cross-sectional investigation assessed animals captured across treatment and diagnostic centres during the post-peak phase of the coronavirus disease pandemic. Among ninety-six captured rodents, molecular testing revealed SARS-CoV-2 ribonucleic acid in nine specimens, establishing an overall viral RNA prevalence of 9.4 percent with a 95 percent confidence interval extending from 5.01 to 16.86 percent. Concurrent serological testing identified anti-SARS-CoV-2 immunoglobulin G antibodies in nine serum samples, also representing a 9.4 percent positivity rate. When combining molecular detection and serological reactivity, the total documented exposure rate reached 15.6 percent, accounting for fifteen individual animals. The findings represent the first confirmed documentation of natural SARS-CoV-2 infection among commensal rodent populations in an African urban environment. The fieldwork was structured across three specialized medical centers in Brazzaville that were central to municipal COVID-19 diagnosis and inpatient clinical care. Inpatient treatment for suspected and confirmed human infections was provided at the Brazzaville University Hospital and the Albert Leyono Municipal Clinic, whereas the National Public Health Laboratory functioned as the primary national screening facility. Traps were baited with standard local food attractants including bread, cassava, sardines, peanut butter, and bananas, operating for two nights per week at each testing location. Trapped animals were transported daily to the Directorate General of Livestock for standardized necropsy processing. Under local field constraints and limited anesthesia availability during the pandemic, animals underwent gradual inhalation anesthesia using diethyl ether in sealed observation containers before cervical dislocation, followed by immediate collection of cardiac blood and organ tissues for -80 °C storage. Morphological and taxonomic identification classified the ninety-six captured specimens into four distinct rodent categories across the three surveyed medical institutions. The black rat, Rattus rattus, was the overwhelmingly predominant species captured, comprising eighty individuals, followed by thirteen Asian house rats, Rattus tanezumi, two common house mice, Mus musculus, and a single specimen identified as Sundamys species. In terms of geographical origin, fifty-four animals originated from the National Public Health Laboratory, thirty-nine from Brazzaville University Hospital, and three from the Albert Leyono Municipal Clinic. The demographic breakdown showed a male-to-female sex ratio of seventy-eight males to eighteen females, while age categorization determined seventy-seven juveniles, thirteen mature adults, and six rodents whose age could not be reliably established. Systematic post-mortem physical examinations revealed macroscopic lesions in only two rodents overall, consisting of superficial abscesses on Rat-50 and scrotal enlargement with hepatic necrosis on Rat-39, but notably none of the SARS-CoV-2 positive animals exhibited gross pathological signs. Discover more Shop Rabbit Food Book Care Services Study Biology Infection infections Molecular testing for viral shedding focused directly on large intestine tissue specimens, which were homogenized using mechanical cold-grinding in biosafety cabinets prior to chemical extraction. Laboratory scientists disrupted approximately thirty milligrams of intestinal tissue per specimen at fifty hertz using a automated TissueLyser platform before performing total ribonucleic acid purification via the commercial NucleoSpin RNA protocol. Viral RNA was confirmed in nine animals, distributed unevenly among the three capture environments: seven of thirty-nine rodents at Brazzaville University Hospital tested positive, representing an institutional rate of 17.9 percent, one of three at the Albert Leyono Municipal Clinic tested positive for 33.3 percent, and one of fifty-four at the National Public Health Laboratory tested positive for 1.8 percent. Evaluating positive molecular detections by species demonstrated that seven of eighty Rattus rattus carried viral RNA for an 8.7 percent rate, alongside one of thirteen Rattus tanezumi at 7.7 percent and one of two Mus musculus at 50 percent. Demographic analysis revealed an age association, as all nine RT-qPCR positive individuals were juvenile rodents, whereas zero adult specimens tested positive for viral genetic material. Sex comparisons indicated that viral RNA was identified in eight of seventy-eight male rodents, representing 10.3 percent, and in one of eighteen female rodents, representing 5.5 percent. However, statistical evaluation using Fisher’s exact test revealed that sex differences in infection were not statistically significant, yielding a p-value of 1. Conversely, when examining total infection and exposure across species combining molecular and serological detection, statistical comparisons indicated a significant difference with a p-value of 0.01, driven by both house mice testing positive compared to lower frequencies in rat cohorts. Discover more Check Symptoms infection Get Health Tips To expand diagnostic sensitivity on intestinal samples displaying lower viral loads, investigators implemented a nested reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction targeting the RNA-dependent RNA polymerase gene. This secondary enzymatic protocol successfully amplified the expected 420-base-pair target amplicon in six of the nine specimens that had previously demonstrated positivity on initial real-time screening assays. The amplified fragments underwent electrophoresis on ethidium-bromide-stained agarose gels and were subsequently subjected to Sanger dideoxy sequencing covering approximately 1.3 to 1.8 percent of the total SARS-CoV-2 genome. Comparative sequence alignments against international reference archives using the BlastN tool demonstrated that the recovered rodent sequences shared between 98 percent and 99 percent nucleotide identity with the original ancestral NC_045512 reference strain from Wuhan. Maximum likelihood phylogenetic reconstruction confirmed that all six generated rodent sequence fragments clustered indisputably within the Betacoronavirus genus alongside circulating SARS-CoV-2 lineages rather than representing divergent endemic animal coronaviruses. Phylogenetic analysis using the Nextclade classification tool established substantial lineage diversity among the six sequenced rodent RdRp fragments, mirroring lineages that had actively circulated among human patients in the Republic of the Congo. Two additional rats captured in October and December 2022 at the university hospital clustered within clade 20B and lineage B.1.1.277. Omicron variants were also recovered, including clade 21K lineage BA.1.1 from a university hospital rat and clade 22B lineage BA.5.1.34 from a house mouse taken at the municipal clinic in May 2022. Serological evaluation of serum samples collected via cardiac puncture employed a multiplexed microsphere immunoassay conducted on a Luminex Magpix instrument to quantify circulating immunoglobulin G antibodies. The assay evaluated specific humoral responses against three distinct recombinant viral targets, including the receptor-binding domain, the full trimeric spike glycoprotein, and the intrinsically disordered region of the nucleocapsid protein. Cutoff values for positive antibody binding were established mathematically at three standard deviations above background levels observed in unexposed laboratory-reared control rodents, ensuring specificity benchmarks of 99.8 percent in rats and 96.8 percent in mice. Nine of the ninety-six tested serum samples exhibited antibody levels above established diagnostic thresholds, matching the overall 9.4 percent rate observed in molecular intestinal assays. Positive serological reactivity was detected in five black rats, two Asian house rats, and two house mice across all three collection facilities, comprising one animal at the university hospital, two at the municipal clinic, and six at the public health laboratory. Integrating molecular and serological results permitted investigators to stratify the fifteen exposed animals into three discrete biological infection profiles reflecting different temporal phases of exposure. Two individuals, specifically one house mouse and one black rat, tested positive for both intestinal viral RNA and serum antibodies, displaying a dual-positive profile consistent with active, ongoing, or persistent viral replication. Six rodents, including one Asian house rat and five black rats, exhibited viral RNA in intestinal tissue but lacked detectable circulating antibodies, representing acute recent infections sampled prior to the maturation of a systemic humoral immune response. Finally, six rodents, comprising one mouse, two Asian house rats, and three black rats, demonstrated anti-SARS-CoV-2 antibodies in serum despite testing negative for viral RNA by polymerase chain reaction, indicating cleared historical infections or transient past exposures. This profile heterogeneity indicates that transmission within the rodent population occurred asynchronously over several months rather than representing an isolated cluster event. Because urban rodents dwell at the immediate interface of human activity, exposure within medical centers likely occurred through indirect environmental pathways such as contact with contaminated personal protective equipment, hospital wastewater, or discarded clinical solid waste. The detection of viral RNA and specific antibodies across multiple commensal species aligns with previous international surveys in Europe, the Americas, and Asia that recorded rodent seroprevalence rates ranging from 0.4 percent to 16.5 percent. The total absence of macroscopic clinical symptoms in infected wild rodents suggests that natural transmission may involve lower viral inocula or effective host viral clearance, while supporting the capacity of commensal mammals to act as asymptomatic maintenance reservoirs. Furthermore, the identification of circulating Omicron variants alongside earlier lineages demonstrates the continuous susceptibility of peridomestic rodents to evolving human strains. The study authors emphasize that reinforcing waste segregation, environmental sanitation, and coordinated One Health microbiological surveillance within healthcare facilities remains vital to preventing persistent animal reservoirs and mitigating reverse-zoonotic transmission risks. records.content: 巴基斯坦2023—2024年SARS-CoV-2 Omicron毒株的系统发育多样性特征及多国比较基因组流行病学研究 《Brazilian Journal of Microbiology》:Retrospective analysis of SARS-CoV-2 Omicron strains (2023 to 2024) from Pakistan reveals differential phylogenetic diversity across genomes compared with other countries 【字体: 大 中 小 】 时间:2026年11月21日 来源:Brazilian Journal of Microbiology 2.1 为了促进科学的传播,生物通采集了这篇文章 订阅BioHot点这里解锁原文链接推送! “畅读会员”点此登录查看原文链接 Medicine and Public Health - Research Paper Open access 背景 SARS-CoV-2 Omicron变异株在2023年和2024年持续在全球涌现,然而来自巴基斯坦的基因组流行病学(genomic epidemiology)研究仍较为有限。研究人员通过研究全基因组系统发育多样性(phylogenetic diversity)和熵(entropy),将巴基斯坦的Omicron变异株与西方国家美国、英国、法国以及邻国印度的分离株进行了比较。 方法 研究人员研究了2023年1月至2024年9月期间收集的SARS-CoV-2基因组。对于巴基斯坦,研究人员还重点分析了阿迦汗大学医院(Aga Khan University Hospital)的逆转录聚合酶链反应(Reverse Transcription Polymerase Chain Reaction, RT-PCR)阳性样本。统计分析将P值<0.05视为具有统计学意义。基于基因组的谱系分配(lineage assignment)使用Pangolin v4.4 pangoLEARN完成,分支分配(clade assignment)使用Nextclade v3.5.0完成。序列使用MAFFT v7.505进行比对,并使用IQ-TREE v2.2.0构建最大似然系统发育树(maximum-likelihood phylogenetic tree)。确定替换率(substitution rates)和Shannon基因组熵(Shannon genomic entropy)。 结果 在巴基斯坦,XBB.1及其亚变体在2023年占主导地位,而JN.1及其亚变体持续至2024年。尽管KP.2、LB.1和LA.1等变体在2024年中期出现,JN.1仍保持主导地位。相比之下,美国、英国和法国的SARS-CoV-2在2024年9月显示出从XBB.1.5过渡到JN.1和KP.3.3。值得注意的是,JN.1毒株在印度持续存在至2024年。巴基斯坦的基因组替换率为0.467E-04(95CI: 3.29E-04–6.04E-04),与美国、英国和法国的替换率相似,但高于印度。巴基斯坦SARS-CoV-2平均位点熵(mean positional entropy)为0.0324,高于其他国家(0.01–0.013)。 结论 研究人员描述了巴基斯坦Omicron的多样性,XBB和JN.1谱系(lineage)毒株持续存在至2024年。这些发现为SARS-CoV-2基因组进化提供了见解。可用的相对较小的基因组序列限制了与全球毒株替换率的比较。需要扩大监测范围以了解大流行毒株的本地传播情况。 2019年末,严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2(Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2, SARS-CoV-2)引发的2019冠状病毒病(Coronavirus Disease 2019, COVID-19)迅速演变为全球大流行。该病毒在进化过程中产生了大量变异株,其传播能力、免疫逃逸潜力及疾病严重程度各不相同。各国监测能力差异显著,巴基斯坦的病毒检测能力在2021年达到每日约46,500次的峰值,远低于美国同期水平。2023年3月,世界卫生组织(World Health Organization, WHO)宣布新冠疫情紧急状态结束,但Omicron变异株仍在持续进化,其中变异株JN.1及多种监测中的变异株(Variants Under Monitoring, VUM)至今仍在流行。然而,关于2023年之后巴基斯坦流行菌株的基因组流行病学信息仍十分有限。巴基斯坦于2021年2月引入COVID-19疫苗,主要为灭活病毒疫苗,而mRNA疫苗供应有限。为填补后疫情时期的研究空白,并探究巴基斯坦与具备强大基因组监测能力的西方国家及邻国之间的进化差异,研究人员开展了此项研究,旨在描述2023至2024年巴基斯坦SARS-CoV-2 Omicron变异株的流行特征,并通过系统发育与熵分析进行跨国比较。 欢迎下载【ADC药物研发与生产解决方案】,查看各阶段相关工艺流程技术细节! 领 取 本研究采用回顾性研究设计,数据主要来源于全球共享所有流感数据倡议组织(Global Initiative on Sharing All Influenza Data, GISAID)数据库(2023年1月至2024年9月)及巴基斯坦阿迦汗大学医院(Aga Khan University Hospital, AKUH)的RT-PCR阳性鼻咽拭子样本队列。关键技术方法包括:基于Pangolin v4.4 pangoLEARN的谱系分配和Nextclade v3.5.0的分支分配;使用MAFFT v7.505进行多序列比对(multiple sequence alignment),IQ-TREE v2.2.0构建最大似然系统发育树;通过Augur流程进行时间分辨系统发育分析、替换率(substitution rate)估算及Shannon熵(Shannon entropy)计算;采用随机子抽样策略对各国序列进行标准化处理(每月最多300条序列);使用IBM SPSS Statistics version 26.0进行统计学分析。 巴基斯坦SARS-CoV-2基因组流行病学 研究人员对GISAID数据库中的976条巴基斯坦基因组进行分析,最终935条符合纳入标准。结果显示,2023年3月XBB.1.19.1(21%)和XBB.1.9.1(18%)占主导,随后GW.5和GW.5.1在2023年8月上升,FL.1和FY.5于2023年10月出现。2024年3月,JN.1(46%)和JN.1.18(31%)成为主要毒株,尽管KP.2、LB.1和LA.1在2024年中期出现,JN.1仍持续主导至2024年9月。共鉴定出86种独特变异株,其中13种相对频率超过20%。 AKUH检测的SARS-CoV-2样本描述 对AKUH在2023年1月至2024年9月间282例RT-PCR阳性样本的回顾显示,19至50岁人群占54%,大于50岁者占44%,1至18岁儿童占3%。卡方检验(Chi-squared test)表明,研究期间SARS-CoV-2病例数无显著线性变化趋势(χ2 = 7.83, df = 1, P = 0.097),月际波动呈现波状传播特征。 AKUH的SARS-CoV-2基因组流行病学 对213条AKUH测序基因组分析发现,样本94.8%来自信德省(Sindh),主要包括喀奇(Karachi)和海得拉巴(Hyderabad)。主要优势毒株包括XBB.1(23.9%)、FL(13.2%)、XBB.1.5(9.9%)、JN(9.4%)、XBB.1.9(8.5%)、EG(6.6%)、GW(6.1%)和XCC(6.1%)。Fisher精确检验(Fisher's exact test)显示谱系与性别(p = 0.537)及住院状态(inpatient/outpatient status)无显著关联,卡方独立性检验显示谱系与年龄组亦无显著关联(χ2(1.64), p = 0.44)。热图分析揭示,2023年第三季度FY.5上升至25%,2024年第三季度JN变体频率达100%。 巴基斯坦SARS-CoV-2的系统发育分析 基于780条巴基斯坦序列构建的时间分辨最大似然系统发育树显示,巴基斯坦序列分散于多个分支,呈现明显的谱系多样化。从23A(XBB.1.1.5)演化出23B、23D、23E和23F分支;从23I(BA.2.86)锐化出现导致24A(JN.1)、24H(HK.3)和24F(XEC)分支。研究估算替换速率为4.67E-04(95CI: 3.29E-04–6.04E-04)每位点每年。Shannon熵分析显示,平均位点熵为0.0324,突变频率在刺突(Spike, S)基因区域最高,其次为ORF1ab。 巴基斯坦、美国、英国、法国和印度基因组的比较 跨国比较纳入美国(n=286,135)、英国(n=54,574)、法国(n=32,137)和印度(n=14,734)序列,经随机子抽样后分别为6,301、6,244、6,301和3,436条。2023年1月至6月,XBB.1.5在美国占主导(84%);2023年末至2024年初,JN.1在全球快速扩张,至2024年9月成为美国、英国和法国的优势毒株,但在印度JN.1.1仍持续循环。系统发育树显示,上簇(23B、23D、23E、23F)代表XBB亚谱系扩展,下簇(24A、24C、24E)代表JN.1及其后代谱系;巴基斯坦序列在XBB相关分支中持续存在至2024年,而美国、英国和法国在2024年已主要过渡到JN.1衍生分支。替换率方面,美国、英国和法国介于4.4E-04至5.22E-04,与巴基斯坦相似(Cochran's Q检验:Q = 3.91, df = 3, p = 0.27, I2 = 23%),但显著高于印度(6.92E-05,95CI: 0–1.4E-04)。平均位点熵美国为0.0100,英国为0.0107,法国为0.0105,印度为0.0129,均低于巴基斯坦的0.0324。 研究人员指出,巴基斯坦JN.1毒株持续存在至2024年第三季度,与欧洲、北美多数国家JN.1被KP.2.3和KP.3.1.1取代的趋势不同,这一模式与南亚部分地区的观察相似。高平均位点熵可能源于相对较小的数据集,但S基因区域的高突变频率提示病毒在免疫压力下的活跃进化。研究还注意到,巴基斯坦主要使用灭活疫苗,而mRNA疫苗供应有限,这可能在塑造当地进化动态中发挥作用。与印度相比,巴基斯坦毒株替换率较高,但印度数据集的置信区间较宽(下限为0),提示需进一步研究。研究局限性包括:巴基斯坦检测能力受限,基因组监测仅限于少数机构,可用基因组序列数量相对较少,且数据集未包含临床严重程度和疫苗接种状态信息,因此无法将菌株变异与临床表型相关联。
