2019年末,严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2(Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2, SARS-CoV-2)引发的2019冠状病毒病(Coronavirus Disease 2019, COVID-19)迅速演变为全球大流行。该病毒在进化过程中产生了大量变异株,其传播能力、免疫逃逸潜力及疾病严重程度各不相同。各国监测能力差异显著,巴基斯坦的病毒检测能力在2021年达到每日约46,500次的峰值,远低于美国同期水平。2023年3月,世界卫生组织(World Health Organization, records.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Monday, November 23, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health T Cells Drive Sustained Inflammation Three Years After COVID-19 Infection by November 21, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 2 mins read 0 T Cells Drive Sustained Inflammation Three Years After COVID-19 Infection Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram A longitudinal study tracking forty-seven convalescent individuals reveals that immune dysregulation and chronic inflammation can persist for up to three years following COVID-19 infection. Published as a brief report in Immunity & Inflammation, the investigation maps the long-term peripheral immune landscape during recovery. The researchers tracked immune remodeling to clarify how unresolved immune system disruptions contribute to prolonged convalescence and persistent post-infection symptoms. To characterize cellular changes over the extended follow-up window, the research team applied single-cell RNA sequencing alongside multiplex cytokine profiling. These complementary analytical techniques permitted comprehensive profiling of peripheral blood samples collected from the patient cohort across the three-year period. By examining transcriptomic alterations at single-cell resolution alongside circulating cytokine measurements, the authors evaluated how circulating immune cell populations and inflammatory mediators evolve over time following SARS-CoV-2 infection. Discover more Read Med Journals Read Health News Check Symptoms The peripheral immune profiles demonstrated sustained immune dysregulation characterized by chronic inflammatory activity and defective cellular restoration. Specifically, patients exhibited impaired recovery across multiple specific lymphocyte compartments, including naïve CD4-positive T cells, naïve CD8-positive T cells, and SLC4A10-positive mucosal-associated invariant T cells. The authors observed that this protracted failure to reconstitute essential naïve and innate-like T cell subsets exhibits cellular features reminiscent of immunosenescence. Discover more Study Biology Find Treatments Get Rapid Tests COVID-19 Notably, Th17 cells, rather than monocytes, emerged as primary drivers of chronic inflammation beyond one year of follow-up. Detailed transcriptomic characterization distinguished two functionally divergent subsets within the circulating Th17 compartment: RORC-positive Th17 cells and LTB-positive Th17 cells. While the frequency of RORC-positive Th17 cells correlated negatively with circulating inflammatory cytokine concentrations, the LTB-positive subset displayed prominent proinflammatory features and correlated positively with patient-reported long COVID symptoms. Molecular analyses further identified potential soluble signals supporting the lingering pathogenic T cell population. Convalescent patients maintained sustained elevation of two specific inflammatory mediators, S100A8 and interleukin-16, throughout the follow-up period. According to the study findings, the prolonged systemic presence of S100A8 and interleukin-16 may actively contribute to the ongoing persistence of proinflammatory LTB-positive Th17 cells in these individuals. Overall, the three-year longitudinal analysis establishes an in-depth map of peripheral immune remodeling during recovery from COVID-19. The findings synthesize published research on viral persistence, immune activation, and histopathological alterations across diverse organ systems in post-acute infection settings. Long COVID, also designated as post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2, is estimated to affect approximately 10 to 20 percent of individuals after initial viral infection. While the condition imposes a substantial global health burden, its underlying pathophysiological mechanisms remain incompletely understood. To evaluate how viral remnants and host responses contribute to persistent illness, the researchers synthesized observations from symptom-defined post-acute patients alongside wider post-acute cohorts, autopsy series, and case investigations. The research was conducted under PRISMA guidelines and registered with PROSPERO under registration code CRD420261403869. Investigators systematically searched four major electronic databases, specifically PubMed, Scopus, EMBASE, and Cochrane CENTRAL. Eligible publications were subsequently categorized into four distinct methodological strata: symptom-defined Long COVID evaluated at or beyond 12 weeks, broader post-acute or mixed patient groups lacking consistent diagnostic timing, dedicated autopsy investigations, and isolated case or fetal reports. Discover more Read Med Journals Study Biology Check Symptoms Infectious infection Across the surveyed literature, 45 individual reports met the criteria for inclusion in the narrative synthesis. Among these, 16 reports analyzed symptom-defined Long COVID at or after 12 weeks, 23 examined post-acute or mixed cohorts, three were autopsy investigations, and three documented isolated case or fetal presentations. Individual study quality was examined using Joanna Briggs Institute appraisal checklists to evaluate item-level characteristics rather than to assign definitive certainty-of-evidence grades. The synthesized results demonstrated marked variability in the identification of viral components across anatomical sites. Detection of viral genomic sequences and viral proteins differed significantly based on participant selection criteria, post-infection sampling intervals, tissue specimen types, and specific analytical assays employed. The authors noted that a single aggregate participant total could not be determined across the review because of overlapping patient cohorts, repeated biospecimen sampling, and outcome-specific analytical denominators. Histopathological assessments revealed structural and cellular abnormalities across evaluated tissues, characterized primarily by inflammatory infiltrates, fibrosis, and vascular injury. However, the systematic analysis determined that establishing clear causal attribution between these tissue changes and Long COVID was substantially constrained by several confounding elements. These limitations included acute illness severity, clinical indications driving tissue biopsies, underlying patient comorbidities, and the widespread absence of appropriate comparator groups. Overall, the review supports notable biological heterogeneity following SARS-CoV-2 infection, encompassing persistent viral fragments, immune dysregulation, vascular injury, and maladaptive tissue repair pathways. Despite these observations, critical questions remain unanswered, as organ-specific prevalence, a distinct hierarchy of tissue tropism, replication-competent reservoirs, and the therapeutic superiority of antiviral or immunomodulatory regimens could not be established from the available evidence. Discover more infectious Get Rapid Tests Find Lung Care Read Health News Find Treatments To resolve these lingering clinical and biological uncertainties, the authors concluded that future research requires standardized Long COVID diagnostic definitions alongside fully representative patient cohorts. Further investigation must also incorporate validated detection assays, properly matched control comparators, and longitudinal study designs capable of directly linking measurable biological markers with clinical health outcomes. records.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Monday, November 23, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health SARS-CoV-2 Antibodies Detected in European Moose and Asian Golden Cat by November 18, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 2 mins read 0 SARS-CoV-2 Antibodies Detected in European Moose and Asian Golden Cat Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram Researchers conducting serological investigations in zoological institutions across Germany have detected antibodies against severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) in a European moose (Alces alces) and an Asian golden cat (Catopuma temminckii). The discovery directly expands the documented host range of the virus among captive mammalian species following the progression of the human COVID-19 pandemic. The serological investigation examined the presence of specific antibodies to address growing concerns regarding the potential establishment of novel animal reservoirs. Investigators collected and analyzed serum samples from 123 individual mammals housed in various zoological institutions throughout Germany between December 2019 and January 2025. All surveyed animals had maintained documented direct or indirect contact with humans, including facility visitors and attending zoo staff members. The sampled zoological cohort incorporated a broad taxonomic selection to survey viral exposure across multiple mammalian orders. Members of the order Artiodactyla represented the largest portion of the tested population with 59 individual animals, alongside 54 specimens representing the order Carnivora. The remaining surveyed institution animals comprised seven representatives of the order Proboscidea, two perissodactyls, and a single rodent. To evaluate serological status across this diverse taxonomic group, all collected serum samples underwent systematic testing using two standardized laboratory methods. The researchers utilized a species-independent commercial surrogate virus neutralization test (sVNT) alongside a multispecies receptor-binding domain (RBD)-based enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). With only two exceptions among the 123 sampled mammals, all specimens tested consistently negative across both the sVNT and the RBD-based ELISA assays. The positive findings were restricted to the European moose, which was sampled in 2020, and the Asian golden cat, sampled in 2021. Both individual animals demonstrated detectable antibodies in both laboratory tests, confirming prior exposure to the virus during the ongoing pandemic period. The identification of reactive antibodies in these two species expands the known animal host range of the pathogen following its spread in humans. The authors conclude that continued pathogen monitoring and health surveillance across both captive and wild animal populations remain essential. Such monitoring is necessary for understanding the actual host range, assessing potential reservoir formation, and clarifying broader implications for both animal and public health. records.content_title: COVID-19 and the teenage brain: Why the severity of symptoms may matter
records.content: As the teenage brain undergoes critical developmental changes, researchers examine whether the frequency and severity of past COVID-19 infections are linked to the cognitive skills adolescents rely on in the classroom and everyday life. Study: Adolescents’ COVID-19 history is associated with their cognitive performance. Image Credit: vectorfusionart / Shutterstock In a recent study published in the journal Scientific Reports , researchers investigated the associations between coronavirus disease 2019 ( COVID-19 ) infection history, symptom severity, and cognitive, motor, and psychomotor performance among adolescents, including potential gender differences. Adolescents reporting more severe COVID-19 symptoms scored lower in logical reasoning and numerical ability, with lower verbal scores particularly evident among girls. Neither infection occurrence nor frequency was significantly linked to cognitive performance. The research was conducted by scientists from the Faculty of Psychology at Karl Landsteiner University of Health Sciences, in collaboration with the WKNÖ Educational Information Centre in Austria. Background COVID-19 is caused by severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 ( SARS-CoV-2 ) and has been linked to cognitive impairment in adults, such as difficulties with memory, attention, and executive function. Its potential effects during adolescence remain less understood. This period of development is characterized by substantial brain restructuring, particularly in the areas responsible for higher-order cognitive functions. Previous research has also identified cognitive difficulties among children and young people following infection. School absences, sleep disturbances, and persistent symptoms such as fatigue may contribute to these difficulties. Further large-scale research using standardized cognitive assessments is needed to clarify these associations and potential gender differences. About the study The researchers conducted a cross-sectional study involving 3,860 adolescents aged 12–16 (mean age: 13.5 years) living in Lower Austria, Austria. Data were collected from April to October 2024 through the Austrian Institute for Economic Development’s vocational information center. Girls accounted for 47.4% of the sample. Participants and their parents provided written informed consent, and the assessments were conducted in German under standardized conditions. Study participants self-reported their COVID-19 history, including whether they had been infected, how often, and the severity of their worst illness. Symptom severity was assessed using a 9-point scale, ranging from mild illness with minimal symptoms to severe illness requiring hospitalization. Cognitive abilities were measured using the Inventory for Testing Cognitive Capabilities ( INT ), which assessed verbal ability, logical reasoning, numerical ability, visual-spatial ability, and long-term memory. The Motorische Leistungsserie ( MLS ) assessed fine motor ability by measuring tapping speed, gross and fine finger dexterity, and hand guidance errors. A computerized choice-reaction test was used to evaluate the ability to process information during mentally demanding tasks, with the researchers focusing on errors. This custom assessment had not been independently validated. The researchers used multivariate regression and gradient-boosting machine-learning models to examine associations, identify gender differences, and detect potential nonlinear patterns. The models accounted for age, gender, and school type, and the regression analysis incorporated corrections for multiple statistical comparisons. Study results Among the 3,860 participants, 83.9% reported having experienced at least one SARS-CoV-2 infection. On average, previously infected participants who provided infection counts reported around 1.6 infections. The average symptom severity score among those who rated their symptoms was 2.9 out of 9. The researchers found no significant gender differences in infection prevalence, infection frequency, or symptom severity. The multivariate regression analysis showed that COVID-19 symptom severity was associated with lower performance in logical reasoning, numerical ability, and verbal ability among girls, who served as the reference group in the primary statistical model. For logical reasoning, this relationship did not differ significantly between boys and girls. Lower numerical ability was also associated with increasing symptom severity when both genders were analyzed together. The association appeared considerably weaker among boys, but the gender difference was not statistically significant. Verbal ability demonstrated a gender-specific association. More severe COVID-19 symptoms were linked to lower verbal scores among girls, with a significantly weaker relationship among boys. After cognitive scores were converted to a standardized scale (mean = 100, SD = 15), the estimated differences between the least and most severe symptom courses ranged from approximately 3 to 7 points. The gaps were 5.4 points for reasoning and 2.9 points for numerical ability across boys and girls combined, and 7.2 points for verbal ability among girls. These estimates represent differences in specific cognitive domains rather than measured declines in overall IQ . The authors considered these differences potentially meaningful for adolescents’ cognitive and educational development. The machine-learning analysis largely supported the findings on reasoning and verbal ability. Using gradient boosting and SHapley Additive exPlanations ( SHAP ) values, the researchers identified reasoning, verbal ability, fine finger dexterity, and long-term memory as domains for which symptom severity contributed most to model predictions. Numerical ability followed closely. The models suggested possible nonlinear relationships between symptom severity, fine finger dexterity, and long-term memory, but neither outcome showed statistically significant associations in the linear regression models. In particular, fine finger dexterity appeared to deteriorate at the upper end of the severity scale. These exploratory findings need confirmation. After accounting for demographic and educational variables, COVID-19-related factors explained less than an additional 1% of the variation in each performance outcome. The primary regression analysis found no significant links between symptom severity and motor or psychomotor abilities. eBook: Advancing infectious disease vaccine development eBook Curious how to enhance your current infectious disease research? This eBook from hVIVO offers insight into getting smarter workflows, stronger evidence, and faster regulatory alignment. Download the latest edition Additional sensitivity analyses identified logical reasoning as the ability most consistently linked to symptom severity. After excluding participants with the highest severity ratings (7 or above), the association with reasoning remained statistically significant. The association with numerical ability and the gender-specific verbal finding no longer met the threshold for statistical significance, but the estimates remained similar. Infection frequency was not significantly associated with any of the ten performance outcomes. Infection occurrence was also unrelated to performance across the ten domains tested in the primary regression analysis. How much cognitive variation did COVID-19 history explain? Percentage of variation in cognitive and fine motor performance explained by demographic, educational and COVID-19-related factors. Age, gender and school type Additional COVID-19-related variation Performance outcome Variation explained (R2) COVID-19 contribution Total Verbal ability 0.45% 10.8% Logical reasoning 0.58% 8.7% Numerical ability 0.28% 6.7% Visual-spatial ability 0.25% 5.6% Fine finger dexterity 0.15% 4.1% Long-term memory 0.08% 3.6% 0% 3% 6% 9% 12% Interpretation: COVID-19-related predictors explained less than 1% of the variation in each performance outcome after accounting for demographic and educational factors. Note: The additional COVID-19 contribution represents the percentage-point increase in explained variance, not the percentage of cognitive ability lost. Minor differences in totals reflect rounding in the original publication. The findings do not establish causality. Six selected performance outcomes are presented. Source: Willinger, D., Wunderl, S., & Stieger, S. (2026). Adolescents’ COVID-19 history is associated with their cognitive performance. Scientific Reports, Table 2. DOI: 10.1038/s41598-026-80578-y. Conclusion The findings suggest that adolescents experiencing more severe COVID-19 symptoms may perform less well in certain cognitive domains, particularly reasoning and numerical skills, with lower verbal ability specifically associated with symptom severity among girls. Systemic inflammation and disruption of developing neural networks are possible explanations, but the study did not investigate these mechanisms directly. The cross-sectional design, self-reported infection histories, and lack of pre-infection cognitive assessments prevent causal conclusions. Pre-existing differences in cognitive ability or related factors could also have contributed to more severe illness. The researchers lacked precise infection dates, vaccination histories, and information on pre-existing health conditions, pubertal development, and detailed socioeconomic circumstances. School closures, social isolation, and mental health difficulties may also have influenced cognitive performance. The researchers called for longitudinal studies and confirmation in independent international populations to establish whether these associations reflect lasting effects of infection. Further investigations should also examine the underlying biological processes, factors that may make some adolescents more vulnerable, and effective interventions. Identifying cognitive difficulties following more severe infections may help adolescents receive appropriate educational and developmental support

records.content: News Around the World University students were the first to spread new SARS-CoV-2 variants — Nature Fedir Kryshtovskyi 19 November 2026 20:44 In Massachusetts, an analysis of more than 85,000 SARS-CoV-2 genome sequences showed that university students consistently began spreading new genetic variants of the virus first. The highest level of COVID-19 transmission in 2021–2023 was also recorded among school students aged 15–18 and residents of elderly care facilities. Testing data in Massachusetts As Nature reports, researchers combined genomic data with epidemiological information about people with COVID-19, including their age and vaccination status. They used test results collected in Massachusetts from November 2021 to January 2023. Genome sequencing made it possible to track the spread of SARS-CoV-2 variants that emerged during this period. More current news is available on the UA.News Telegram channel Telegram . Risks for workers At the same time, employees of schools, universities and elderly care facilities had approximately the same risk of contracting COVID-19 as people in the communities surrounding these institutions. The authors of the analysis also found that booster vaccinations reduced the transmission of SARS-CoV-2, including the Omicron BA.1 variant, which began circulating in Massachusetts in late 2021. The study results were published on November 19, 2026, in the journal Cell. Epidemiologist Bill Hanage of the Harvard School of Public Health called the scale of the work an impressive example of the capabilities of population genomics. Read us on Download our app

records.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Monday, November 23, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Repeated Mild SARS-CoV-2 Infections Impair Synaptic Integrity and Worsen Pathology in Mice by November 18, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 2 mins read 0 Repeated Mild SARS-CoV-2 Infections Impair Synaptic Integrity and Worsen Pathology in Mice Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram Sequential mild respiratory infections with distinct variants of SARS-CoV-2 led to a consistent reduction in hippocampal synaptic integrity in mice and accelerated the accumulation of amyloid plaques in an Alzheimer’s disease model. Investigating how repeated respiratory viral exposures influence the brain, researchers found that these neurological changes occurred without detectable shifts in the quantity or activation states of the central nervous system’s primary immune cells. The study addressed the lung-brain axis, an interconnected communication network between the respiratory system and the central nervous system that has drawn intense interest amid long-term complications from COVID-19. Following the emergence of SARS-CoV-2, millions of individuals developed lingering post-infection symptoms collectively known as long-COVID, with cognitive impairment, fatigue, and brain fog among the most common manifestations. In addition, clinical observations have suggested that SARS-CoV-2 exposure may elevate the risk of developing neurodegenerative disorders such as Alzheimer’s disease, though the biological mechanisms connecting recurrent respiratory infections to brain pathology have remained poorly understood. To investigate these mechanisms, the researchers utilized wild-type and knock-in AppNL-G-F Alzheimer mice crossed into a K18-hACE2 background. The animals were infected sequentially with two antigenically distinct variants of SARS-CoV-2, establishing an experimental protocol designed to reflect the repeated exposures encountered by human populations over successive waves of the pandemic. Discover more Study Biology infection Infections Check Symptoms infections Two weeks following the second viral exposure, the investigators assessed the brain tissue for signs of neuroinflammation and cellular reactivity. The analyses revealed no notable changes in either the total cell numbers or the reactive states of microglial cells and astrocytes, the brain’s primary immune cells, indicating that overt glial activation was not maintained at this post-exposure interval. Despite the absence of measurable microglial and astrocyte reactivity, the infected animals exhibited a consistent reduction in synaptic integrity specifically localized to the hippocampus. Furthermore, in the AppNL-G-F Alzheimer mice, the sequential infections caused an increased accumulation of amyloid plaques, a primary pathological hallmark of Alzheimer’s disease, demonstrating that recurrent mild infections exacerbated underlying disease features in genetically predisposed animals. The authors concluded that recurrent mild SARS-CoV-2 infections can impair neuronal function and worsen brain pathology in susceptible animal models. These findings emphasize the importance of the lung-brain axis in evaluating the prolonged neurological consequences of respiratory viral infections and suggest that individuals predisposed to neurodegenerative conditions may possess heightened vulnerability to repeated viral exposure. India World Sport Entertainment Data Health Opinion Science Premium Videos Podcast Photos Visual Stories Specials TH Explains eBooks TH Games Newsletters Lit For Life The Huddle Home Opinion Lead COVID-19 lessons should inform response to air pollution Tackling air pollution already attracts considerable expenditure, but allocations do not consistently reflect the greatest health risks Updated - November 19, 2026 01:08 pm IST Soumya Swaminathan,Dr Chandrakant Lahariya 4 / 4 New READ LATER SEE ALL Remove People stand on the banks of the Yamuna on a smoggy morning as air pollution spikes in New Delhi on November 13, 2026. | Photo Credit: Reuters There is an uncanny similarity between Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), the virus responsible for the COVID-19 pandemic, and air pollution. During the pandemic, the virus entered our bodies through the air we breathed; harmful particulate matter and toxic gases enter through the same respiratory route. Additionally, both damage multiple organs, including the lungs, heart and brain. Yet, while COVID-19 prompted an unprecedented emergency national response, air pollution continues to be treated largely as a seasonal inconvenience. The harmful effects of air pollution are well-established. An adult takes approximately 20,000–25,000 breaths daily, meaning that even a relatively miniscule worsening of air quality can have substantial health consequences over time. This alone should make improving the quality of air an urgent public health priority. Unlike COVID-19, which was recognised as a public health emergency of international concern, air pollution in India receives limited policy attention despite being a longstanding, year-round threat. The State of Global Air 2025 report estimated that more than two million deaths in India in 2023 were attributable to air pollution, including household and ambient exposure. Beyond premature mortality, millions also experience pollution-related illnesses and hospitalisations. A burden of this magnitude demands urgent national attention. Air pollution is primarily seen as a respiratory issue. In reality, it is far more than a respiratory health concern; it contributes to cardiovascular disease, stroke, chronic respiratory disorders, lung cancer and diabetes. Evidence also links it to exposure to dementia and other neurological disorders. Pregnant women and unborn and young children face extended risks which can affect birth outcomes, lung development and cognitive development, with consequences extending into adulthood. There is also a compelling ethical argument for sustained and decisive government action when it comes to tackling air pollution. Exposure to outdoor air pollution is largely involuntary, and individuals have little to no choice over the air they breathe. This burden is deeply unequal: poorer households, outdoor workers and children often face greater exposure while having fewer resources to protect themselves. records.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Monday, November 23, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Severe COVID-19 Alters Hepatic Autophagy Markers Despite Absent Hepatocyte ACE2 Receptors by November 20, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 6 mins read 0 Severe COVID-19 Alters Hepatic Autophagy Markers Despite Absent Hepatocyte ACE2 Receptors Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram Post-mortem tissue examinations of patients who succumbed to fatal respiratory failure during severe COVID-19 have revealed marked histopathological alterations in liver tissue accompanied by significant shifts in the expression profiles of key autophagy-associated and mitochondrial proteins. The investigation, conducted on an autopsy cohort of individuals who died of severe pulmonary infection, documented detectable SARS-CoV-2 viral proteins within hepatic parenchyma despite the confirmed absence of angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 receptors on the surface of hepatocytes. Alongside these structural and viral observations, researchers identified an upregulation of the autophagosome assembly protein Beclin-1 and the outer mitochondrial membrane marker TOMM20, concurrent with a significant decrease in the autophagy receptor p62 and divergent patterns of microtubule-associated protein light chain 3 immunoreactivity. These findings demonstrate that severe systemic coronavirus infection induces substantive hepatic stress and perturbs the steady-state abundance of regulatory proteins governing intracellular recycling and organelle maintenance, providing vital pathological insights into extrapulmonary manifestations of the disease. Although severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 primarily targets the respiratory tract, clinical practice throughout the pandemic established that the disease frequently precipitates systemic complications and multi-organ impairment, including hepatic dysfunction. The physiological mechanisms mediating liver injury have remained unresolved, largely because hepatocytes express low or negligible baseline levels of angiotensin-converting enzyme 2, which serves as the canonical receptor for viral uptake. While endothelial cells and cholangiocytes within the hepatic microvasculature possess recognized receptor density, the routes by which viral proteins enter hepatocytes and provoke downstream cellular stress have prompted detailed scientific inquiry. In addition to potential multi-organ failure driven by systemic inflammatory responses and cytokine elevation, experimental models have suggested that alternative cellular entry factors and metabolic remodeling events might permit viral engagement with liver cells. Determining whether liver tissue from deceased patients exhibited direct viral presence and whether intracellular degradation pathways were altered represented the principal rationale for undertaking comprehensive post-mortem tissue analyses. Discover more Get Rapid Tests Read Med Journals Read Health News To investigate these questions under rigorous conditions, investigators analyzed liver specimens collected between March 2020 and March 2022 from twenty deceased COVID-19 patients at the Department of Pathology, Forensic and Insurance Medicine at Semmelweis University in Budapest, Hungary. The cohort comprised twelve male and eight female patients with a median age of sixty-six years, in whom fatal respiratory failure accounted for ninety percent of deaths, followed by cardiovascular complications and sepsis accompanied by multi-organ failure. Ante-mortem reverse transcription-polymerase chain reaction testing confirming nasopharyngeal SARS-CoV-2 sequences and low-dose chest computed tomography scans established eligibility. To distinguish infection-specific cellular consequences from non-specific agonal hypoxia and critical illness, the study implemented a matched case-control design comparing these cases with deceased patients suffering from acute respiratory distress syndrome who tested negative for the virus. Both cohorts underwent standardized ten-day courses of invasive mechanical ventilation applying high positive end-expiratory pressure regimens and experienced severe, documented agonal hypoxia before death under tightly standardized pre-analytical autopsy protocols. Discover more Study Biology Study Anatomy COVID COVID-19 Standardization of pre-analytical tissue handling represented a foundational methodological priority designed to prevent post-mortem autolytic artifacts from distorting cellular marker evaluations. The autopsy protocol maintained closely matched post-mortem intervals, averaging 4.5 hours among COVID-19 fatalities and 4.2 hours among the non-COVID controls. Following death, bodies were immediately transferred to cold storage at four degrees Celsius, yielding short cold ischemia times of 1.0 hour and 1.2 hours, respectively. All retrieved liver tissue samples underwent identical fixation in ten percent neutral buffered formalin for forty-eight hours before routine paraffin embedding. Patients were excluded if viral status had been verified solely by rapid antigen testing without molecular polymerase chain reaction confirmation, if they were younger than eighteen years of age, or if they had received pharmaceutical agents known to alter autophagic pathways, including chloroquine, remdesivir, or systemic corticosteroid therapies, thereby ensuring that observed cellular phenotypes reflected genuine pathological states rather than confounding therapeutic interventions. Comprehensive laboratory evaluations recorded upon hospital admission revealed distinct systemic inflammatory profiles that separated the COVID-19 autopsy cohort from non-COVID acute respiratory distress syndrome controls. Patients in the COVID-19 cohort presented with significantly higher median serum concentrations of interleukin-6, reaching 79.9 picograms per milliliter compared to 45.87 picograms per milliliter in the control group, as well as significantly elevated tumor necrosis factor-alpha levels of 8.79 picograms per milliliter compared to 5.65 picograms per milliliter. The deceased COVID-19 patients were also significantly younger, with a median age of sixty-six years compared to seventy-two years in the control group. Admission testing demonstrated elevated C-reactive protein, procalcitonin, lactate dehydrogenase, and D-dimer across patients, while serum alanine aminotransferase and aspartate aminotransferase indicated modest hepatocellular stress. These systemic inflammatory markers documented the intense acute-phase immune activation and widespread circulatory stress present throughout the disease course preceding terminal respiratory arrest. Histopathological assessment conducted by three independent hepatopathology specialists identified a spectrum of structural injuries across the formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded liver sections stained with hematoxylin and eosin as well as periodic acid-Schiff reactions. Structural examinations revealed varying degrees of hepatic steatosis, microvascular endothelial dysfunction, sinusoidal dilatation with vascular congestion, and focal fibrin deposition distributed throughout the tissue architecture. Consensus grading confirmed that while parenchymal damage was evident, severe injury did not occur uniformly, with pronounced liver injury detected in approximately half of the analyzed cases. Notably, traditional angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 immunostaining was negative on healthy hepatocyte surfaces, confirming that hepatic cellular injury and viral uptake occurred independently of standard receptor abundance. These morphological observations confirmed that severe pulmonary SARS-CoV-2 infection routinely associates with circulatory disturbances, vascular compromise, and localized parenchymal disruption within the liver capillary network. Despite the lack of detectable hepatocyte angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 expression, immunohistochemical and molecular assays successfully identified SARS-CoV-2 structural proteins within the liver tissue blocks. Specific monoclonal antibodies directed against the viral nucleocapsid protein and the spike S1 subunit produced unmistakable positive signals in hepatic tissue sections. To evaluate potential alternative entry pathways responsible for internalizing viral particles into receptor-deficient liver cells, the investigators conducted double fluorescent immunohistochemistry examining cell surface heparan sulfate proteoglycans, specifically focusing on syndecan interactions. The fluorescent imaging demonstrated an extensive, statistically significant spatial overlap between the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein and heparan sulfate throughout liver tissue regions, characterized by a Spearman rank correlation coefficient of r equals 0.9345 with a significance level of p equals 0.00675. This strong physical co-localization suggests that cell-surface heparan sulfate chains may participate in binding and concentrating viral particles at the hepatocyte surface, potentially facilitating cellular uptake without requiring classical receptor engagement. Parallel semi-quantitative immunohistochemical analysis revealed pronounced disturbances in the steady-state abundance of regulatory proteins orchestrating the host autophagic machinery. Autophagy is a conserved intracellular catabolic mechanism that encapsulates damaged organelles, aggregated proteins, and invading pathogens within double-membrane autophagosomes for delivery to lysosomes. In the COVID-19 liver specimens, Beclin-1, a multi-domain protein component of the class III phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase complex that initiates autophagosome assembly from pre-autophagic membrane components, exhibited a marked increase in both the percentage of positive cells and semi-quantitative H-scores. In contrast, the selective autophagy receptor p62, also known as sequestosome-1, which binds polyubiquitinated cargo and links it to autophagosomal membranes, showed significantly reduced overall immunoreactivity, occasionally displaying atypical nuclear localization or clustering around lipid droplets. Microtubule-associated protein light chain 3 displayed divergent patterns, exhibiting disparities between the proportion of immunopositive cells and overall staining intensity, reflecting intricate reorganization rather than uniform pathway activation. Concurrently, the mitochondrial outer membrane marker TOMM20 demonstrated prominent elevations in immunoreactivity across the COVID-19 liver tissue sections, showing particularly intense staining within hepatocytes located adjacent to central veins. The translocase of the outer mitochondrial membrane 20 functions as an essential structural receptor responsible for recognizing and importing nuclear-encoded precursor proteins into the mitochondrial matrix, serving as an established histological marker for mitochondrial density, spatial distribution, and organelle turnover. While elevated TOMM20 staining indicates substantial alterations in mitochondrial content and localization under severe viral infection, the authors emphasized that static protein abundance cannot be interpreted as direct evidence of accelerated mitophagic clearance. Because the degradation of damaged mitochondria necessitates coordinated autophagosomal sequestration and fusion with acidic lysosomes, the increased presence of TOMM20 primarily indicates profound organelle stress, potential mitochondrial accumulation, or altered organellar homeostasis during fatal systemic infection. The authors underscored several methodological limitations inherent to autopsy-based investigations that govern the biological interpretation of their findings. Foremost among these considerations is that static immunohistochemical detection of structural proteins like LC3, p62, Beclin-1, and TOMM20 reflects stationary protein levels rather than real-time autophagic flux or the rate of functional mitophagic degradation, which would require dynamic interventional assays such as lysosomal protease inhibition. Furthermore, while SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid and spike proteins were detected within hepatic specimens, antibody-based protein identification does not prove productive viral replication, as in situ molecular replication assays and viable viral isolation were not executed. Finally, the observed spatial correlation between viral spike proteins and heparan sulfate remains an observational association that cannot establish a direct causal entry mechanism in human tissues. Consequently, the investigators concluded that while severe COVID-19 undeniably associates with disrupted hepatic organelle homeostasis and altered autophagy protein expression, targeted functional and dynamic cell-culture studies remain essential to delineate the precise molecular pathways involved. records.content: New tool guides earlier care of long COVID cases Improved patient follow-up and a clinical support tool help primary-care teams better diagnose and manage persistent symptoms. Media Contact: Colleen Steelquist - csteelqu@uw.edu In national surveys, less than one-third of family medicine and internal medicine doctors report feeling “very prepared” to recognize and evaluate patients with long COVID. Dr. Betsy O’Kane, a family medicine doctor at UW Medicine Primary Care at Shoreline, considered herself one of the underprepared. “I’d see patients who had a history of COVID come into the clinic with symptoms that were hard to understand and confusing,” she said. “I really had no experience with long COVID and how to manage it.” Defined as persistent symptoms lasting at least three months following COVID-19 infection, long COVID is a prevalent public health problem. The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services estimates that about 18 million people in the United States have experienced it. About 5.3% to 7.6% of the U.S. adult population has active long COVID. It most commonly causes fatigue, cognitive impairment and malaise after exertion — symptoms worsen after physical or mental activity. It also causes problems with several organ systems. Symptoms can emerge, persist, resolve and reemerge weeks or years later. There is no definitive diagnostic test. O’Kane’s patients often were unaware that their persistent health concerns might stem from a prior COVID infection. If she suspected a patient had long COVID, she could refer them to the UW Medicine Long COVID Clinic, but its limited capacity, as with such clinics nationwide, meant it could take up to a year for patients to be seen. O’Kane collaborated on a novel solution with Dr. Anita Chopra, clinical associate professor of medicine at the University of Washington School of Medicine, and Dr. Andrew White, UW Medicine's assistant chief clinical information officer, with support from an interdisciplinary team. Using the Epic electronic health record platform, they created a two-pronged approach: a post-COVID patient survey to identify potential long COVID cases, and a decision-making tool to help frontline clinicians. “After they have COVID, some patients deal with chronic fatigue, dizziness, a racing heart or other symptoms, but they don't have a name to identify it,” said Chopra. “By the time it hits them that this might be long COVID, months have passed and they do not get the appropriate care.” The collaborators first created a four-question symptom survey for UW Medicine Primary Care patients diagnosed with COVID, emailed three months after diagnosis. If the patient identifies persistent symptoms, an alert is sent to their care team so a follow-up appointment can be offered. The team also built an Epic-embedded clinical decision tool to enable primary-care clinicians to more easily identify and manage the complex symptoms of their patients with long COVID. Because a typical primary-care visit leaves little time to look up evolving guidance, the tool utilizes SmartSets — intuitive and interactive prompts for initial and subsequent visits. It helps clinicians: - ask patients questions that elicit useful details - identify tests and imaging to order - steer symptom management - provide counseling and information - generate after-visit patient instructions The tool helps translate rapidly emerging scientific evidence into a usable format at the fingertips of primary-care clinicians. O’Kane said patients benefit when their long COVID symptoms are addressed more quickly and thoroughly. “First, when a patient feels like they've been heard and the clinician understands their concerns, that is incredibly powerful. Then you're starting to work as a team to create a path for the patient’s recovery,” she said. “Second, rather than waiting a year to get into the Long COVID Clinic before doing lab tests and trialing medications, we can do that ahead of time. If we find a problem, we can treat that immediately. We can try physical therapy or send them to a pulmonologist,” O’Kane continued. “If they’re still not making good progress, then we’re sending the really complex patients to the specialty clinic instead of those who could get better more quickly by being managed by their primary-care clinician.” The project was piloted at three primary-care sites this fall. Early user evaluation showed clinicians’ confidence in diagnosing long COVID increased from 18% to 65%. Confidence in managing the illness rose from 0% to 59%. All of the responding clinicians, regardless of specialty or years of experience, reported that the tool and guidelines were useful. The tool and SmartSets, available to all Epic users nationwide in December, can be accessed by typing “long COVID” into the SmartSets search field. The project was supported by the Washington State Department of Health and Pfizer. For details about UW Medicine, please see our About page

records.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Monday, November 23, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Exercise Rehabilitation Improves Walking Capacity in Long COVID Cardiopulmonary Recovery by November 18, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 6 mins read 0 Exercise Rehabilitation Improves Walking Capacity in Long COVID Cardiopulmonary Recovery Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram Structured exercise-based rehabilitation programs can significantly enhance functional walking capacity and cardiopulmonary fitness among adults recovering from persistent cardiopulmonary and cardiovascular impairments associated with long-term coronavirus disease 2019, according to a systematic review and exploratory bioinformatics analysis published in Discover Public Health. Drawing together intervention evidence from multiple clinical centers, researchers systematically evaluated randomized controlled trials alongside non-randomized interventional studies published between 2019 and 2025 that examined supervised physical training protocols in post-acute coronavirus populations. Across eight included clinical investigations encompassing a pooled cohort of 578 participants, supervised training regimens consisting of aerobic exertion, progressive resistance activities, combined modalities, and traditional qigong exercises were consistently associated with measurable gains in physical endurance, self-reported vitality, and respiratory comfort. Participants enrolled in structured rehabilitation consistently demonstrated clinically relevant improvements in submaximal exercise tolerance, with distances on the standardized six-minute walk test extending by approximately 70 to 120 meters and peak oxygen consumption increasing by 10 to 18 percent across evaluated cohorts. The clinical motivation for the synthesis centers on the enduring multisystemic consequences that frequently linger well beyond the acute phase of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 infection. Persistent post-acute sequelae, broadly classified as long COVID or post-COVID-19 conditions, often manifest as debilitating exercise intolerance, persistent dyspnea, muscle weakness, chest discomfort, autonomic instability, and generalized fatigue that severely restrict daily domestic routines and occupational return. In severe acute illness, viral infiltration via angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 receptors, acute systemic inflammation, hypoxemia, and electrolyte disruptions can trigger acute myocardial injury, ventricular arrhythmias, pericardial inflammation, and thromboembolic vascular events. When hospitalized patients transition out of intensive care or acute inpatient wards, profound physical deconditioning frequently compounds residual cardiopulmonary limitations. Although physical activity is widely understood to bolster general immune resilience and cardiovascular health, the scientific literature addressing structured exercise therapy for post-infectious cardiovascular sequelae has historically remained fragmented, prompting the review team to synthesize the therapeutic parameters, physiological adaptations, and clinical uncertainties characterizing current exercise prescription. To rigorously identify and appraise the published evidence, the research team implemented a comprehensive systematic literature search across PubMed, Scopus, and the Web of Science Core Collection spanning from initial pandemic outbreaks through December 31, 2025. Following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines, investigators mapped search strings incorporating controlled Medical Subject Headings and comprehensive free-text terms addressing post-COVID conditions, cardiopulmonary impairments, and exercise-based therapeutic modalities. The authors developed and finalized an analytical protocol deposited in the Open Science Framework repository to govern eligibility decisions. Interventions of interest comprised supervised outpatient, inpatient, or home-based rehabilitation programs delivering aerobic exercise, muscular resistance training, inspiratory muscle conditioning, or multimodal regimens to individuals experiencing post-acute viral sequelae. Independent reviewers screened thousands of database records, extracting study designs, participant demographics, training parameters, monitoring protocols, and validated clinical outcomes, while simultaneously conducting rigorous risk-of-bias assessments using established Cochrane evaluation frameworks to gauge potential methodological confounding. Discover more Book Workouts Get Rapid Tests Read Med Journals Read Health News Shop Walking Shoes The final synthesis incorporated eight distinct intervention studies that investigated diverse therapeutic approaches tailored for individuals experiencing post-COVID cardiopulmonary complications. Among these, five studies examined combined exercise programs integrating continuous aerobic exertion and progressive resistance training, one trial compared isolated endurance training against concurrent endurance-resistance conditioning and non-exercising controls, one investigation delivered high-intensity interval training on cycle ergometers alongside resistance exercises, and one randomized clinical trial tested a specialized hospital-based qigong and acupressure rehabilitation protocol. Across these heterogeneous investigations, rehabilitation regimens typically scheduled supervised exercise sessions two to three times per week over intervention windows lasting between two and twelve weeks. While some programs enrolled non-hospitalized individuals with post-COVID-19 syndrome, others evaluated cohorts discharged following prolonged inpatient management or invasive mechanical ventilation, thereby capturing a broad cross-section of post-infectious functional limitation and varying baselines of residual physiological deficit. Functional capacity improvements represented the most pronounced and consistent clinical finding identified across the reviewed intervention studies. In a highlighted quasi-experimental pre-and-post evaluation conducted by Araújo and colleagues involving 26 recovering adults, twelve sessions of moderate-intensity outpatient rehabilitation combining aerobic and resistance training yielded a mean increase in six-minute walk distance of 70.57 meters, rising from 419.47 to 490.04 meters. The authors emphasized that this observed change substantially exceeded the widely recognized minimum clinically important difference threshold of 30.5 meters established for cardiopulmonary rehabilitation cohorts. Similarly, an inpatient evaluation conducted by Mińko and colleagues observed an average improvement of 120 meters on the six-minute walk test following two to six weeks of comprehensive daily conditioning encompassing respiratory drills and aerobic-resistance exercises. These functional gains coincided with measurable reductions in post-exercise dyspnea, improved post-exertional peripheral oxygen saturation, and marked gains in lower-limb strength, illustrating meaningful recoveries in ambulatory autonomy. Direct physiological assessments of cardiopulmonary performance further substantiated positive adaptations in cardiorespiratory efficiency across several evaluated cohorts. In the randomized COVID-Rehab trial conducted by Besnier and colleagues involving 40 individuals with long COVID, participants completing an eight-week supervised cardiopulmonary rehabilitation program achieved a significant improvement in peak oxygen uptake of 2.7 milliliters per kilogram per minute, compared with a negligible change of 0.3 milliliters per kilogram per minute among control participants. Araújo and co-workers likewise observed that maximal exercise tolerance increased significantly, with mean peak oxygen consumption advancing by 3.56 milliliters per kilogram per minute, reflecting an 18.62 percent increase alongside an extended duration to reach peak exertion and a favorable reduction in the ventilatory equivalent slope for carbon dioxide. Additionally, Douin and colleagues recorded an 18 percent elevation in maximal oxygen uptake and a 26 percent increase in maximal workload among post-COVID patients undergoing cardiopulmonary exercise testing, accompanied by a 10 percent reduction in exercise-induced hyperventilation. Alongside objective physiological metrics, the reviewed rehabilitation programs produced widespread reductions in patient-reported symptom burden, fatigue severity, and psychological distress. Across multiple trials utilizing validated psychometric instruments, including the Fatigue Assessment Scale, the Fatigue Severity Scale, the 12-Item Short Form Survey, and the Patient Health Questionnaire-9, enrolled participants reported meaningful alleviations in physical weariness and perceived depressive symptoms. In the randomized clinical investigation conducted by Liu and colleagues examining 128 hospitalized patients with severe illness, the introduction of a qigong exercise and acupressure rehabilitation program produced superior improvements on the modified Medical Research Council and modified Borg dyspnea scales relative to standard therapy alone. Participants assigned to the qigong intervention also experienced significantly shorter cough durations and shortened hospital stays, demonstrating that gentle, symptom-limited movement modalities can offer therapeutic utility even during acute and subacute recovery phases within clinical environments. To provide exploratory biological context for the severe inflammatory environments that frequently precede chronic post-viral deconditioning, the investigators conducted a secondary bioinformatics exploration utilizing a publicly available transcriptomic microarray dataset derived from primary mouse bone marrow-derived macrophages stimulated with inflammatory cytokines. Differential expression analysis performed through R Bioconductor packages identified 544 significantly dysregulated transcripts meeting stringent threshold criteria, comprising 235 upregulated and 309 downregulated genes. Subsequent protein-protein interaction network construction prioritized 72 central hub genes exhibiting elevated degree and centrality metrics. Cross-species orthologue conversion and functional enrichment against comprehensive human pathway libraries linked these hub networks to tumor necrosis factor signaling, interleukin cascades, interferon responses, apoptosis, and lipid metabolism. However, the study authors explicitly noted that this exploratory computational analysis represents hypothesis-generating preclinical context; it was derived from in vitro murine cells rather than human cardiac biopsies and did not measure direct exercise interventions, meaning it cannot demonstrate that physical training directly alters these molecular pathways in recovering humans. Crucially, the review authors cautioned clinicians against adopting aggressive or rigid exercise prescriptions, emphasizing that post-COVID cardiopulmonary rehabilitation requires individualized, symptom-guided titration rather than fixed heart-rate targets. Due to the potential occurrence of cardiovascular drift—a physiological phenomenon characterized by progressive heart-rate elevation during sustained exercise despite constant mechanical workloads—as well as latent autonomic dysregulation, chronotropic incompetence, and orthostatic intolerance, predetermined heart-rate reserve calculations should serve only as approximate initial guides rather than absolute training ceilings. Exercise sessions must be actively governed by continuous multidimensional monitoring, incorporating workload adjustments, ratings of perceived exertion, respiratory symptom ratings, arterial oxygen saturation, blood pressure responses, and heart-rate recovery trajectories. Clinicians are urged to pause or adapt sessions if disproportional fatigue, oxygen desaturation, or abnormal hemodynamic fluctuations emerge, ensuring that patients avoid triggering severe post-exertional symptom exacerbation or unmasking occult myocardial vulnerability. Despite the generally encouraging findings, the review authors emphasized that the overall certainty of evidence remains low to very low across all primary outcome domains due to substantial methodological limitations. The evidence base is characterized by small sample sizes, brief follow-up periods, considerable heterogeneity in training modalities, and an absence of non-exercise control groups in several quasi-experimental designs, which prevents researchers from definitively distinguishing exercise-mediated adaptations from spontaneous natural recovery, concurrent pharmacological therapies, or repeated testing effects. Furthermore, none of the included clinical trials mandated confirmed structural cardiac damage as an inclusion criterion or evaluated direct myocardial imaging endpoints, meaning the observed improvements reflect functional and cardiopulmonary rehabilitation rather than proven reversal of intrinsic cardiac pathology. The authors concluded that while individualized, supervised, symptom-limited exercise appears feasible and beneficial within comprehensive post-COVID care frameworks, rigorously controlled trials with objective cardiovascular phenotypes and extended longitudinal monitoring remain essential. 尽管RNA依赖性RNA聚合酶(RdRp)在RNA病毒的复制中起着至关重要的作用,但严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2型(SARS-CoV-2)的RdRp Nsp12的致病效应仍未得到充分认识。在此,研究人员构建了一种条件性敲入小鼠模型,能够在体内诱导表达SARS-CoV-2 Nsp12(以下简称Nsp12小鼠)。在Nsp12小鼠中,可检测到的Nsp12表达需要在体外和体内均与整合应激反应(integrated stress response,ISR)抑制剂联合处理。在抑制ISR的情况下,Nsp12诱导并未引起明显肺炎或主要免疫细胞群的显著改变。有趣的是,基于机器学习的行为学分析显示,雌性Nsp12小鼠的自发运动活性降低,而雄性小鼠则无此变化。这一行为表型可通过RdRp抑制剂EIDD-2801治疗而显著改善。同样,透射电子显微镜(transmission electron microscopy,TEM)显示Nsp12小鼠心脏和小脑中出现线粒体异常,而Nsp12在这些器官中并未检测到表达。这些异常可被EIDD-2801治疗所减轻,提示Nsp12的RdRp活性可能参与线粒体功能障碍的发生。综上所述,这些结果表明病毒RdRp Nsp12可能通过器官间通讯诱导全身性组织功能障碍。尽管仍需进一步研究阐明这些跨器官效应的确切机制,并鉴定Nsp12表达细胞释放的介质,但研究人员的发现为单一病毒因子SARS-CoV-2 RdRp Nsp12在体内不依赖于复制的致病效应开辟了新的研究途径。 建立可诱导表达SARS-CoV-2 Nsp12的条件性敲入小鼠模型:揭示复制非依赖性致病效应 瑞孚迪自动化解决方案>>领 取 一、研究背景与科学问题 病毒感染后持续存在的多种症候群,如SARS-CoV-2、埃博拉病毒和登革热病毒感染后出现的长期后遗症,被统称为感染后急性期综合征(post-acute infection syndromes,PAIS),归类于感染相关性慢性疾病(infection-associated chronic illnesses,IACIs)。其中,长新冠(long COVID,LC)患者即使在急性感染康复后仍经历持续且常致衰弱的症状,包括疲劳、肌痛性脑脊髓炎/慢性疲劳综合征(myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome,ME/CFS)、劳累后不适(postexertional malaise,PEM)、心律失常、体位性心动过速综合征(postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome,POTS)、自主神经功能障碍以及脑雾等认知损害。值得注意的是,即使初始感染程度为轻至中度,这些症状也可能出现,提示LC的发病机制并非单纯由急性期免疫炎症反应驱动。临床研究显示,LC患者存在免疫应答和细胞因子谱等宿主因素的持续紊乱,且女性受影响更为显著;女性LC患者中较低的睾酮水平预示着更重的总体症状负担,提示性激素在LC病理生理学中发挥作用。 SARS-CoV-2属于冠状病毒科,是一种具有约30 kbp基因组RNA的正链RNA病毒。在感染的宿主细胞中,SARS-CoV-2利用病毒和宿主因子翻译病毒RNA并复制其RNA基因组。其中,Nsp12与Nsp7和Nsp8共同构成RNA依赖性RNA聚合酶(RNA-dependent RNA polymerase,RdRp)复合物,对SARS-CoV-2的复制和增殖至关重要。然而,Nsp12对宿主细胞的致病效应在很大程度上仍未得到探索。近期研究表明,Nsp12可与宿主mRNA结合,可能影响选择性翻译或宿主RNA代谢;此外,丙型肝炎病毒(hepatitis C virus,HCV)的RdRp NS5B可产生小分子双链RNA,激活I型干扰素(type I interferon,IFN)信号并参与组织损伤。这些观察提出了病毒RdRp蛋白可能通过其经典基因组复制功能之外的方式参与宿主导向病理过程的可能性。尽管SARS-CoV-2的致病机制通常归因于病毒复制及由此产生的宿主反应,但Nsp12单独是否足以在体内诱导不依赖于复制的致病效应仍属未知。为此,研究人员建立了可诱导的条件性敲入(conditional knock-in,cKI)小鼠模型,表达SARS-CoV-2 RdRp Nsp12,以探究该单一病毒因子是否足以在体内独立于病毒复制诱导系统性组织功能障碍。 二、研究内容与主要结论 研究人员构建了Rosa26-LSL-Nsp12 cKI小鼠品系(简称Nsp12小鼠),通过将LoxP-Stop-LoxP(LSL)序列及下游Nsp12 cDNA插入Rosa26位点实现条件性表达,并与Sftpc-CreERT2小鼠杂交获得肺特异性诱导表达的CreERT2;Nsp12小鼠。研究发现,即使在Cre介导重组后,宿主整合应激反应(integrated stress response,ISR)仍可抑制Nsp12翻译,因此可检测的Nsp12蛋白表达需要在体外和体内均联合ISR抑制剂(ISRi)处理。通过荧光免疫组织化学(fluorescence immunohistochemistry,FIHC)使用两套独立抗体组合(兔抗Nsp12+小鼠抗Nsp12,以及兔抗Strep tag II+小鼠抗Nsp12)证实了Nsp12在肺泡细胞中的特异性表达。Nsp12诱导未引起明显肺炎或主要免疫细胞群(包括CD4+ T细胞、CD8+ T细胞、NK细胞和NKT细胞)的显著改变。然而,基于DeepLabCut的机器学习多动物追踪行为学分析显示,雌性Nsp12小鼠自发运动活性显著降低,而雄性小鼠无此变化;RdRp抑制剂EIDD-2801(莫诺匹拉韦)可预防这一行为缺陷。透射电子显微镜(TEM)分析显示,Nsp12诱导后小鼠心脏和小脑出现线粒体异常(包括线粒体肿胀、嵴破坏和结构变性),尽管这些器官中未检测到Nsp12蛋白表达。EIDD-2801治疗可减轻这些线粒体异常,心脏中ATP5H(线粒体标志物)表达降低和HIF1α蛋白稳定性增加也支持线粒体功能障碍。此外,Nsp12诱导的线粒体异常和运动活性降低呈现性别依赖性,睾酮补充可部分逆转心脏线粒体异常并改善运动活性降低。体外实验表明,Nsp12在初次分离的原代肺细胞中急性损害线粒体功能(MitoTracker?荧光降低),EIDD-2801及其活性代谢物EIDD-1931可恢复线粒体功能。这些结果表明,Nsp12的RdRp活性可能通过器官间通讯诱导全身性组织功能障碍,为理解SARS-CoV-2 Nsp12在体内的复制非依赖性致病效应提供了新见解。 三、关键技术方法 该研究使用的主要技术方法包括:(1)条件性敲入小鼠模型构建:利用C57BL/6N来源的RENKA胚胎干细胞在Rosa26位点插入LSL-Nsp12序列,与Sftpc-CreERT2小鼠杂交实现肺特异性诱导表达;(2)体内诱导系统:通过TAT-Cre重组酶静脉注射或4-羟基他莫昔芬(4-OHT)诱导CreERT2介导的重组,同时联合ISR抑制剂(ISRIB和A9277)实现Nsp12可检测表达;(3)基于DeepLabCut的机器学习多动物行为学追踪分析,评估自发运动活性;(4)透射电子显微镜(TEM)用于线粒体超微结构分析;(5)流式细胞术用于免疫细胞亚群分析;(6)荧光免疫组织化学(FIHC)结合MitoTracker?染色评估线粒体功能。小鼠品系包括Nsp12小鼠、Sftpc-CreERT2转基因小鼠(JAX #0028054)及C57BL/6NJcl对照小鼠,所有动物实验经广岛大学动物研究委员会批准。 四、研究结果分述 (一)可诱导Nsp12小鼠模型的建立 研究人员构建了Rosa26-LSL-Nsp12条件性敲入小鼠品系,Nsp12翻译在Cre介导重组前被上游STOP序列阻断。初步研究意外发现,即使Cre介导重组后,宿主ISR仍抑制Nsp12翻译,可能作为抗病毒防御机制;因此仅在ISRi联合给药时才能通过FIHC检测到Nsp12蛋白表达。GFP荧光因IRES驱动下游翻译效率低下而无法检测。肺组织FIHC通过两套独立抗体组合确认了Nsp12阳性细胞,且在停止ISRi给药4周和16周后Nsp12表达不可检测。 (二)Nsp12诱导不引起明显肺炎或主要免疫改变 H&E染色显示CreERT2;Nsp12小鼠肺组织无明显病理改变,包括肺炎、纤维化、出血或血栓形成;长期组织学分析也显示肺泡结构完整。流式细胞术分析显示CD4+ T细胞、CD8+ T细胞、NK细胞和NKT细胞频率在Nsp12小鼠和对照小鼠之间无显著差异,表明Nsp12诱导不引起明显肺炎或主要免疫细胞群的显著改变。 (三)雌性小鼠Nsp12诱导后出现运动活性损害 基于DeepLabCut的行为学分析显示,雌性Nsp12小鼠在Nsp12诱导后运动时间和总运动距离显著减少,而EIDD-2801联合治疗可预防这一运动活性降低;雄性小鼠运动活性不受Nsp12诱导影响。在CreERT2;Nsp12雌性小鼠中,4-OHT介导的Nsp12诱导同样导致运动活性显著降低,且EIDD-2801可改善该表型。这表明Nsp12诱导选择性降低雌性小鼠的自发运动活性,且该表型可被RdRp活性抑制所改善。 (四)Nsp12表达在原代肺细胞中诱导线粒体异常 体外实验中,4-OHT或TAT-Cre介导的Nsp12诱导显著降低初次分离的CreERT2;Nsp12肺细胞MitoTracker?荧光,表明Nsp12急性损害线粒体功能。RdRp抑制剂前药中仅EIDD-2801可恢复线粒体功能,而其活性代谢物GS-441524、T-705 ribofuranose和EIDD-1931均能恢复线粒体功能,支持Nsp12 RdRp活性参与线粒体功能障碍。 (五)Nsp12诱导与心脏线粒体异常相关 尽管FIHC未在心脏中检测到Nsp12表达,TEM分析显示Nsp12诱导导致心肌细胞线粒体异质性异常(增大、肿胀、嵴破坏),而EIDD-2801联合治疗可显著减轻这些异常。定量FIHC分析显示Nsp12诱导后心脏ATP5H表达降低,EIDD-2801可减轻ATP5H降低。长期Nsp12诱导后心脏中稳定化HIF1α蛋白水平升高,提示可能向糖酵解代谢转变。 (六)Nsp12诱导与小脑浦肯野神经元线粒体异常相关 Nsp12在小脑中同样不可检测,但TEM分析显示Nsp12诱导后小脑浦肯野细胞线粒体嵴严重破坏,EIDD-2801联合给药可预防线粒体异常的发生。这提示Nsp12诱导与远端器官(包括心脏和小脑)的线粒体异常相关,尽管这些组织中无Nsp12可检测表达。 (七)睾酮补充部分拯救Nsp12诱导的表型 雄性CreERT2;Nsp12小鼠无论是否诱导均未显示可检测的线粒体缺陷。睾酮联合治疗可减轻雌性Nsp12小鼠心脏线粒体异常,并部分改善运动活性降低。这表明睾酮补充可部分减轻Nsp12诱导的心脏线粒体异常和自发运动活性降低。 五、讨论与结论 在讨论部分,研究人员指出Nsp12表达在停止ISRi给药后不可检测,但线粒体异常和ATP5H降低在长期Nsp12诱导后仍持续存在,且HIF1α蛋白水平升高,与LC患者中观察到的糖酵解代谢偏好相似,提示Nsp12诱导启动的线粒体异常可能在Nsp12蛋白不可检测后仍持续存在。关于Nsp12翻译激活ISR的分子机制,研究人员推测SARS-CoV-2 RNA基因组中Nsp12编码区内的-1程序性核糖体移码(programmed ribosomal frameshift,PRF)位点可能通过核糖体碰撞触发ISR,但Nsp12小鼠中的密码子优化Nsp12 cDNA缺乏该位点,机制仍不明确。临床观察支持雄激素信号在LC中的相关性,睾酮除已知免疫调节作用外,可能通过维持线粒体完整性的互补机制影响LC发病。与HCV NS5B的复制非依赖性效应相比,Nsp12缺乏内质网定位结构域,且未观察到明显免疫炎症反应,提示不同病毒RdRp的复制非依赖性效应存在机制差异。线粒体异常在心脏和小脑中检测到而Nsp12蛋白不可检测,提示可能通过器官间通讯介导,潜在介质包括循环损伤相关分子模式(damage-associated molecular patterns,DAMPs)、细胞因子、代谢物和细胞外囊泡。研究局限性包括:使用条件性Nsp12小鼠模型而非真实SARS-CoV-2感染;Nsp12表达需短暂ISR抑制;机制分析主要基于体外原代肺细胞;EIDD-2801的体内保护效应可能受药代动力学因素影响;行为学分析采用群体测试模式;线粒体功能主要通过MitoTracker?染色评估;TEM异常形态异质性难以单参数定量;部分实验样本量较小;睾酮保护效应的机制尚不清楚;需要LC患者中的验证研究。 研究结论:Nsp12表达与主要发生于雌性小鼠的线粒体异常相关,宿主因素如性激素可能影响Nsp12相关线粒体易感性。该条件性Nsp12小鼠模型为研究SARS-CoV-2 RdRp Nsp12在体内的复制非依赖性致病效应提供了有用的实验平台。研究人员推测SARS-CoV-2 RdRp Skip to main content HOME NEWS Government + Politics Ag + Environment Health Care Justice Education Election 2026 Commentary ABOUT SUBSCRIBE DONATE Part of States Newsroom Search Search Government + Politics Ag + Environment Health Care Justice Education Election 2026 15:57 News Story COVID-19 Justice Hy-Vee claims $5 million in losses for non-reimbursed COVID-19 vaccinations Lawsuit: Texas company didn’t properly submit reimbursement claims By Clark Kauffman - November 17, 2026 3:57 pm The Hy-Vee grocery chain is suing a Texas billing company over $5 million worth of COVID-19 vaccines that didn’t qualify for reimbursement by the federal government. This Hy-Vee Pharmacy is located at 410 N. Ankeny Blvd. in Ankeny, Iowa. (Photo via Google Earth) The Hy-Vee grocery chain is suing a Texas billing company over $5 million worth of COVID-19 vaccinations, the cost of which was never reimbursed by the federal government. Hy-Vee Inc. is suing Omnisys, a Texas limited liability company also known as XiFin Pharmacy Solutions, in U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Iowa. Hy-Vee, whose food stores typically include full-service pharmacies, alleges that during the COVID-19 pandemic, the nation’s pharmacies were required, by the federal government, to provide vaccinations at no cost to patients in an effort to stem the spread of the virus. The federal government agreed to reimburse those pharmacies for the cost of administering the vaccinations to the uninsured and the underinsured. Hy-Vee claims $5 million in losses for non-reimbursed COVID-19 vaccinations

by Clark Kauffman, Iowa Capital Dispatch
November 17, 2026

The Hy-Vee grocery chain is suing a Texas billing company over $5 million worth of COVID-19 vaccinations, the cost of which was never reimbursed by the federal government.

Hy-Vee Inc. is suing Omnisys, a Texas limited liability company also known as XiFin Pharmacy Solutions, in U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Iowa.

Hy-Vee, whose food stores typically include full-service pharmacies, alleges that during the COVID-19 pandemic, the nation’s pharmacies were required, by the federal government, to provide vaccinations at no cost to patients in an effort to stem the spread of the virus. The federal government agreed to reimburse those pharmacies for the cost of administering the vaccinations to the uninsured and the underinsured.

Hy-Vee alleges it was eligible to receive $40 per vaccine, and that it administered “hundreds of thousands of COVID vaccinations at no cost to the target patient populations” pursuant to the federal program.

In March 2022, the federal government announced the reimbursement program would stop accepting claims after April 5, 2022, due to concerns that funding for the program was running out.

According to the lawsuit, Hy-Vee and many other pharmacies contracted with Omnisys to act as a “clearinghouse” for the submission of reimbursement claims to the federal government, and paid Omnisys for each claim that the Texas company processed and submitted.

Hy-Vee claims that while most of its claims were accepted and reimbursed, some were rejected, with Omnisys asserting that the reason for some of those rejections was lack of funding for reimbursement.

Through Freedom of Information Act requests, Hy-Vee now alleges, the company learned directly from the federal government that the reimbursement program did not run out of money to pay any eligible claims submitted before the April 5, 2022, deadline. In addition, the information obtained by Hy-Vee indicated that some claims were rejected after being submitted after the deadline.

Hy-Vee’s lawsuit suggests Omnisys is to blame for rejected claims the grocery chair had turned over for processing – although, because Hy-Vee’s court petition is heavily redacted, the precise nature of Omnisys’ alleged failures isn’t clear.

For example, the publicly filed lawsuit states: “Despite receiving claims from Hy-Vee for processing, Omnisys failed to [redacted] ... Omnisys also failed to [redacted] ... Omnisys failed to [redacted], resulting in millions of dollars of losses to Hy-Vee ... On June 23, 2022, Omnisys admitted that it timely received over 100,000 claims from Hy-Vee but failed [redacted].”

Hy-Vee alleges the redacted information, if made public, would violate the terms of confidentiality provisions written into its contract with Omnisys.

The specific allegations concerning Omnisys’ alleged failures, while redacted from public view, fall within two separate categories the lawsuit labels as “late claims” and “unsubmitted claims.” Hy-Vee alleges its own investigation of the matter has “uncovered that Hy-Vee timely submitted more than 150,000 claims to Omnisys that were not reimbursed” due to the Texas company’s alleged failures.

The lawsuit claims Hy-Vee’s total losses exceed $5 million. The grocery chain is suing Omnisys for breach of contract and negligent misrepresentation.

Omnisys / XiFin Pharmacy Solutions has yet to file a response to the lawsuit. Calls and emails to the company’s media relations office and its public relations firm were not immediately returned on Tuesday.

On its website, the company says it is dedicated to “empowering healthcare providers to achieve financial strength,” in part through medical billing services and claims management.
