records.content: You need to enable JavaScript to run this app. Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites Latest videos Latest audio Regions Africa Asia Europe Latin America Middle East North America Germany Topics Climate Equality Health Human Rights Migration Technology Categories Business Science Environment Culture Sports In focus COP31AIUkraine war Latest audioLatest videos Live TV Advertisement Science COVID-19: What role does blood type play? Gudrun Heise 10/15/2020October 15, 2020 A case of COVID-19 can be from mild to severe. Sometimes no symptoms are present, sometimes people die. More and more studies suggest that blood types may play an important role by affecting immune responses. https://p.dw.com/p/3e1pR Copy link Prefer DW on Google Image: picture-alliance/dpa/S. Hoppe Advertisement Why do some people not notice at all that they have contracted the coronavirus, while others require medical treatment — and, in the worst cases, even die? That COVID-19 seems so unpredictable also makes it difficult to find out how many people are actually infected and how many have already built up immunity. The number of unreported cases is correspondingly high. Read more: Coronavirus: Tests show half of people in Italy's Bergamo have antibodies Focus on the blood type Already in June, German and Norwegian researchers analyzed different blood types with regards to COVID-19. They came up with some informative results, which they published in the New England Journal of Medicine. Knowing about Blood Groups To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video 01:37 The researchers investigated the role blood type might play in patients with particularly severe forms of the disease. In the study, the researchers examined 1,610 patients with COVID-19 respiratory failure in Italy and Spain, where the coronavirus hit particularly hard: Milan, Monza, Madrid, San Sebastian, and Barcelona. All patients were struggling with particularly severe cases, and some did not survive. Blood type A means highest risk A first result: People with blood type A seem to be at a particularly high risk of a severe case of COVID-19. In Germany, 43% of the population has this blood type. In the event of coronavirus infection, these individuals might be two times more likely to need an oxygen supply or respirator than people with blood type O: 41% of Germany's population. Read more: Blood test detects more than 50 types of cancer Does the blood type decide the severity of the disease? Image: AFP/S. Avila Blood type O may be able to consider themselves lucky as things stand. Even though they are not protected against an infection, the study shows they have the lowest risk of coming down with a severe case of the disease. People with blood type O- (O negative) also play a special role as blood donors, as they are considered "universal donors" and can help anyone in need of a blood transfusion. Read more: The immune system's fight against the coronavirus Blood types B and AB are not as widespread, making up just 11% and 5% of the population, respectively. According to the study, the likelihood of a severe COVID-19 diagnosis for these groups could lie somewhere between that of people with blood types O or A. More and more studies with similar results Since then, further studies have been added to confirm the original results. On 14 October, two studies appeared in the journal Blood Advances, here and here, which also show less severe symptoms of the disease in people in blood group O. Simultaneously, the Medical University of Graz independently reported aseries of experiments, designed to further investigate the phenomenon. Advertisement Consequences for treatment The results of the studies may help in developing various drug treatments. Researchers have used similar approaches when searching for medication to fight other diseases. In the case of malaria, for example, scientists have established a link between the disease and different blood types. For example, it is now known that people with blood type O very rarely develop severe malaria and are very well-protected against its most severe form. In the case of other diseases, other blood types protect the human body best. For example, with the bubonic plague, people with blood type A showed the mildest symptoms. For a long time, COVID-19 research focused on high-risk patients: Those who have certain preexisting conditions and/or have reached a certain age. Smokers also came under scrutiny as a potentially high-risk group. Now, researchers are looking at a different piece in the coronavirus jigsaw puzzle. Read more: Coronavirus drugs: Can antibodies from survivors help? Note from the editors: This article has been updated since its original publication to reflect information gathered from new scientific studies. Vitamin C: Good for the immune system and for fighting infections A good immune system is always important but it is even more so now, in times of COVID-19. To have one, the body needs enough micronutrients — such as vitamin C. So let's talk about fruit, vegetables and biochemistry. Image: picture-alliance/Zoonar/D. Freigner Eat me! Most mammals can synthesize vitamin C i.e., produce it themselves. But humans can't; we must ingest this water-soluble micronutrient with our food. Vitamin C can be found in kiwis, oranges and grapefruits, but also in vegetables such as brussels sprouts, broccoli and peppers. Unfortunately, it is somewhat heat-sensitive — so be careful when cooking! Image: picture-alliance/Zoonar/S. Schnepf Less mystery, more biochemistry Vitamin C is not just a nice-to-have that is mainly important for the old, the sick and vegans. On the contrary, its biochemical functions are the same and equally important in every body. Vitamin C is one of the micronutrients that, although they do not provide the body with energy, are essential for its basic functions. These include cell metabolism and our defense system. Image: picture-alliance/dpa/F. Gabbert A radical pursuer of radicals As an antioxidant, vitamin C reduces the damage caused by oxygen free radicals to molecules that are essential for the body. These radicals are produced during normal metabolic processes. However, harmful substances such as tobacco quickly lead to oxidative stress and the increased formation of free radicals. This also increases the need for vitamin C. Image: picture-alliance/dpa/W. Rothermel Strawberries to boost enzyme activity The human body doesn't just use the vitamin C of these strawberries to protect against oxygen radicals; the vitamin is also an important cofactor in a number of enzymatic activities, such as the synthesis of the protein collagen, which forms part of tendons, bones, cartilage and the skin. Poor wound healing can thus indicate a vitamin C deficiency. Image: picture-alliance/dpa/F. Rumpenhorst Counterattack with grapefruits The body needs vitamin C to defend itself against infections. As an antioxidant, vitamin C is responsible not only for cell protection; it also goes on the attack in the event of an infection. It stimulates the migration of immune cells, known as neutrophils, to the site of infection, promotes phagocytosis — cellular waste disposal — and kills pathogens. Image: picture-alliance/Panther Media/R. Tsubin Sufficiency beats deficiency Severe vitamin C deficiency can lead to scurvy. Symptoms of this potentially fatal disease are poor wound healing, bruising, loss of hair and teeth and joint pain. To protect against it, 10 milligrams of vitamin C daily are sufficient. Sufficient vitamin C is also associated with a lower risk of high blood pressure, coronary heart disease and strokes. Image: picture-alliance/dpa/B. Pedersen How much is enough? According to the German consumer advice center, the recommended daily intake of vitamin C is 110 mg for men and 95 mg for women. Oregon State University researchers recommend 400 mg per day for all adults. The vitamin is harmless, and if too much is ingested, it is excreted in the urine. Researchers say that whether taken as a dietary supplement or as brussels sprouts, it is the same vitamin C. Image: picture-alliance/dpa/R. India World Sport Entertainment Data Health Opinion Science Premium Videos Podcast Photos Visual Stories Specials TH Explains eBooks TH Games Newsletters Lit For Life The Huddle Home Opinion Lead COVID-19 lessons should inform response to air pollution Tackling air pollution already attracts considerable expenditure, but allocations do not consistently reflect the greatest health risks Updated - November 19, 2026 01:08 pm IST Soumya Swaminathan,Dr Chandrakant Lahariya READ LATER SEE ALL Remove People stand on the banks of the Yamuna on a smoggy morning as air pollution spikes in New Delhi on November 13, 2026. | Photo Credit: Reuters There is an uncanny similarity between Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), the virus responsible for the COVID-19 pandemic, and air pollution. During the pandemic, the virus entered our bodies through the air we breathed; harmful particulate matter and toxic gases enter through the same respiratory route. Additionally, both damage multiple organs, including the lungs, heart and brain. Yet, while COVID-19 prompted an unprecedented emergency national response, air pollution continues to be treated largely as a seasonal inconvenience. The harmful effects of air pollution are well-established. An adult takes approximately 20,000–25,000 breaths daily, meaning that even a relatively miniscule worsening of air quality can have substantial health consequences over time. This alone should make improving the quality of air an urgent public health priority. Unlike COVID-19, which was recognised as a public health emergency of international concern, air pollution in India receives limited policy attention despite being a longstanding, year-round threat. The State of Global Air 2025 report estimated that more than two million deaths in India in 2023 were attributable to air pollution, including household and ambient exposure. Beyond premature mortality, millions also experience pollution-related illnesses and hospitalisations. A burden of this magnitude demands urgent national attention. Air pollution is primarily seen as a respiratory issue. In reality, it is far more than a respiratory health concern; it contributes to cardiovascular disease, stroke, chronic respiratory disorders, lung cancer and diabetes. Evidence also links it to exposure to dementia and other neurological disorders. Pregnant women and unborn and young children face extended risks which can affect birth outcomes, lung development and cognitive development, with consequences extending into adulthood. There is also a compelling ethical argument for sustained and decisive government action when it comes to tackling air pollution. Exposure to outdoor air pollution is largely involuntary, and individuals have little to no choice over the air they breathe. This burden is deeply unequal: poorer households, outdoor workers and children often face greater exposure while having fewer resources to protect themselves. records.content_title: Impact of the COVID-19 Pandemic on Hospital Service Utilization at a Tertiary Care Institute in Central India: A Retrospective Observational Study
records.content: Abstract Background: Hospitals take a substantial share of healthcare system resources, and monitoring service utilization is crucial for performance audit and future planning. COVID-19 pandemic disrupted routine healthcare delivery all over the world, yet significant evidence from tertiary care hospitals in central India is limited. Objectives: The objective of this study was to assess changes in inpatient, surgical, outpatient, and diagnostic service utilization at a tertiary care institute in central India by comparing the one-year period before COVID-19 (1st April 2019 to 31st March 2020) with the COVID-19 pandemic period (April 1, 2020 to March 31, 2021). Methods: A retrospective, observational, record-based pre-post comparative study was conducted at a tertiary care institute in India using de-identified, aggregated administrative data. Monthly data on inpatient admissions and deaths, bed occupancy rate (BOR), bed turnover rate (BTR), average length of stay (ALOS), operation theatre utilization, outpatient department (OPD) attendance, and laboratory and radiodiagnostic service volumes were analysed. Department-level indicators (n = 29) were compared using independent-samples t-tests or Mann-Whitney U test, while paired t-tests and one-way ANOVA were applied where appropriate. A p-value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. The study was reported as per the STROBE (Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology) guidelines. Results: Inpatient admissions declined by 26.8% during the COVID period, while in-hospital deaths increased by 70.5%. Mean BOR and BTR decreased significantly, whereas mean ALOS increased (all p < 0.05). Total operation theatre hours fell from 10,877.8 to 2,953.2 hours (p < 0.001). Overall OPD attendance declined by 63.0% (p < 0.001). Diagnostic utilization decreased overall, with reductions in radiodiagnostic, biochemistry, and pathology services, alongside a 49% increase in microbiology testing. Conclusions: The COVID-19 pandemic caused marked reductions in hospital service utilization, increased inpatient acuity, and a shift in diagnostic workload. These findings underscore the importance of flexible capacity planning, protection of essential non-COVID services, and structured recovery strategies to strengthen hospital resilience. Introduction Hospitals are central constituents of the healthcare system and account for a substantial proportion of healthcare expenditure globally, estimated to range from 40% to 80% of total health spending. As a result, hospital performance and resource utilization remain critical priorities for health system planning and policy decision-making [1,2]. Tertiary care hospitals, in particular, consume a disproportionate share of healthcare budgets owing to the increasing adoption of advanced technologies, expanding service portfolios, and rising public expectations for specialized care [3]. Hospital utilization reflects how resources for healthcare are retrieved and used by a community and is commonly evaluated using standardized specific indicators [4]. Measures such as bed occupancy rate (BOR), bed turnover rate (BTR), and average length of stay (ALOS) serve as quantitative variables of inpatient efficiency, capacity use, and routine patient flow [5]. Similarly, operation theatre utilization rate is an important measure of the efficiency of surgical facilities, with high capital and operational costs linked with operating theatre complexes. These indicators are widely used to support planning of services, workforce allocation, development of infrastructure, and performance monitoring in tertiary care hospital settings [6]. The COVID-19 pandemic imposed an unprecedented burden on health systems worldwide and extensively disrupted routine hospital care services [7,8]. In response to the surge in COVID-19 patients, hospitals reallocated beds, manpower, and critical care resources, deferred elective surgeries, and restricted outpatient services [9,10]. Simultaneously, patient healthcare-seeking behaviour changed due to various factors like lockdowns, transport limitations, and fear of infection [11,12]. Together, these factors resulted in marked reductions in outpatient hospital visits, elective procedures, and diagnostic facilities, while increasing the complexity and intensity of care among hospitalized patients in many such settings [13,14]. Despite the large literature describing pandemic-related healthcare service disruptions, evidence from low- and middle-income countries, particularly from tertiary care institutions in central India, is limited [15]. Moreover, many available studies focus on single service domains, such as outpatient attendance or surgical data, rather than providing a comprehensive assessment across inpatient, surgical, outpatient, and diagnostic facilities using standardized utilization indicators [16,17]. Periodic evaluation of hospital resource utilization using routinely collected administrative data is essential for identifying inadequacies, minimizing wastage of various resources, and strengthening the preparedness for future health system events [18]. A comprehensive assessment of the hospital resource utilization patterns during the COVID-19 period, compared with pre-pandemic levels, can provide actionable insights for hospital administrators and policymakers to guide service recovery and resilience planning [19]. Therefore, the present study aimed to quantify changes in hospital bed utilization, operation theatre functioning, outpatient attendance, and diagnostic facilities workload at a tertiary care institute in central India by comparing the pre-COVID period with the peak COVID-19 period. This study is reported in accordance with the Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology (STROBE) guidelines. Materials & Methods Study design and study setting This was an observational, retrospective, record-based pre-post comparative study conducted at the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), Bhopal, a tertiary care hospital in Madhya Pradesh, India. Hospital service utilization indicators were compared across two defined fiscal periods: the pre-COVID-19 period (April 1, 2019 to March 31, 2020) and the COVID-19 period (April 1, 2020 to March 31, 2021). The COVID-19 pandemic period coincided with nationwide lockdowns, service reorganization, and pandemic-related care delivery changes throughout the world. Data sources and measurement De-identified, aggregated administrative data were obtained from the Medical Records Department, Hospital Management Information System (HMIS), OT logs, outpatient department (OPD) registers, and laboratory and radiodiagnostic departments after due administrative approvals. Data were provided to the investigators without any personal identifiers. The variables were extracted on a monthly basis for each study period. Department-wise inpatient data included monthly admissions and in-hospital deaths, disaggregated by gender, along with key inpatient utilization indicators, namely ALOS, BTR, and BOR. OT utilization was assessed using the total OT hours utilized and the total allocated OT block hours for each department. OT utilization was assessed using the ratio of total operative hours utilized to the total allocated OT hours for each department during the corresponding study period. The resulting percentage represents utilization relative to the allocated theatre time in each period. Monthly outpatient department (OPD) attendance was recorded across broad specialties, super-specialties, AYUSH (Ayurveda, Yoga & Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha, and Homoeopathy), and allied services. Laboratory workload was assessed based on the monthly volume of investigations performed in Biochemistry, Microbiology, and Pathology. Monthly radiodiagnostic workload was recorded by modality, including ultrasonography, X-ray, computed tomography (CT), and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). In addition, the overall monthly surgical workload was quantified in terms of total operative hours. Units of analysis For inpatient service indicators (BOR, BTR, ALOS, and OT utilization rate (OTR)), clinical departments (n = 29) served as the units of analysis. For outpatient and diagnostic services, analyses were conducted at the specialty or service-category level, using aggregated monthly volumes. The calculations for the different variables were done according to the following formulas: (i) BOR = Total inpatient days×100Number of functional beds×Number of days; (ii) BTR = Total discharges (including deaths)Average number of beds; (iii) ALOS = Total inpatient daysTotal discharges (including deaths); (iv) OTR = Total OT hours utilized×100Total allocated OT hours Statistical analysis Data cleaning, data management, and statistical analyses were performed using the Jamovi version 2.5.6 software (www.jamovi.org). Descriptive analysis was done to summarize hospital utilization indicators for the study period. Continuous variables were reported as mean ± standard deviation (SD) or median with interquartile range (IQR) on the basis of distributional characteristics, while number counts were summarized as totals and monthly averages. Normality of continuous variables was assessed through visual inspection and evaluation of distributional assumptions. Comparisons between the two study periods were performed using appropriate parametric and non-parametric tests. The independent-samples t-test was used for normally distributed continuous variables at the department level, while the Mann-Whitney U test was applied to non-normally distributed variables, including OTRs. One-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) was used to assess variations in bed occupancy rates across departments. For specialty-level comparisons of OPD attendance between the two study periods, paired t-tests were performed. Since corresponding clinical departments were evaluated during both study periods, departmental comparisons were treated as paired observations. Paired-samples t-tests were used for normally distributed differences, whereas the Wilcoxon signed-rank test was considered for non-normally distributed paired observations. All statistical tests were two-sided, with a p-value of less than 0.05 considered statistically significant. Effect estimates were interpreted in addition to descriptive trends to observe the magnitude and direction of changes in service utilization. Ethical considerations The study utilized anonymized, aggregated administrative data and involved no direct patient contact. The study was approved by the Institutional Human Ethics Committee, All India Institute of Medical Sciences, Bhopal (approval number: IHEC-LOP/2022/IL012). Individual informed consent was not sought because this retrospective secondary analysis used routinely collected hospital administrative records, involved no direct patient contact, and reported only aggregated, non-identifiable findings. Data confidentiality and governance were maintained throughout all stages of the study. Results Overview of hospital service utilization Across all domains, hospital service utilization declined during the COVID-19 pandemic period compared with the period just before the pandemic. Total inpatient admissions decreased from 21,333 in 2019-20 to 15,607 in 2020-21, representing a reduction of 5,726 (26.8%). Over the same period, total in-hospital deaths increased from 590 to 1,006, corresponding to an increase of 416 (70.5%). The distribution of admissions by gender remained comparable across the two periods, whereas the proportion of male deaths increased modestly. Overall inpatient admissions and deaths are summarized in Table 1. OPD attendance declined substantially during the COVID period. Total OPD visits across all specialties decreased from 493,529 to 183,206, an absolute reduction of 310,323 (63.0%) visits. Inpatient bed utilization indicators Department-level inpatient utilization indicators are presented as means with standard deviations. The mean BOR declined from 59.31% (SD 22.12) in the pre-COVID period to 49.83% (SD 23.61) during the COVID period. Mean BTR decreased from 30.05% (SD 15.78) to 20.41% (SD 14.32). In contrast, mean average length of stay (ALOS) increased from 7.17 days (SD 3.86) to 9.10 days (SD 4.77). Independent-samples t-tests conducted at the department level (n = 29 departments per period) demonstrated statistically significant differences between the pre-COVID and COVID periods for BOR, BTR, and ALOS (Table 2). BOR and BTR were significantly lower during the COVID period, whereas ALOS was significantly higher. The 95% confidence intervals for the mean differences indicated non-overlap for BTR and ALOS. Department-wise variation in bed occupancy One-way ANOVA was used to assess heterogeneity in BOR across departments. The analysis demonstrated statistically significant variation in BOR among the 29 clinical departments (F (28,29) = 4.62, p < 0.001). The estimated effect size (η2) indicated a large between-department effect, suggesting differential impacts of the COVID period on bed occupancy across clinical services. OT utilization OT utilization showed a marked decline during the COVID period. Total OT hours utilized decreased from 10,877.8 (15.25%) hours in 2019-20 to 2,953.2 (4.29%) hours in 2020-21. As OT utilization percentages were non-normally distributed, department-level utilization rates were compared using the Mann-Whitney U test. A statistically significant reduction in OT utilization was observed during the COVID period (U = 41.0, z = −4.21, p < 0.001). The magnitude of the difference was large, as indicated by the rank biserial correlation (r = 0.74). Department-level OT utilization data for selected surgical specialties are presented in Table 3. Outpatient services Specialty-level OPD attendance was analysed using paired comparisons of monthly averages. Paired t-tests demonstrated a statistically significant reduction in OPD attendance during the COVID period compared with the pre-COVID period (paired t (35) = 6.88, p < 0.001), with a large effect size (Cohen’s d = 1.15). Aggregate OPD attendance data are shown in Table 4. Diagnostic services Laboratory and radiodiagnostic service utilization demonstrated heterogeneous trends during the COVID period. Total laboratory test volumes declined from 485,299 in 2019-20 to 363,181 in 2020-21, representing a reduction of 122,118 (25%). Biochemistry and Pathology services recorded reductions of 113,481 (45%) and 56,774 (43%), respectively, while Microbiology test volumes increased by 48,137 (49%). Laboratory service utilization data are summarized in Table 5. Radiodiagnostic service volumes decreased overall by 49,229 (39%), from 124,819 investigations in 2019-20 to 75,590 in 2020-21. Reductions were observed across all imaging modalities, including ultrasonography 13,681 (−50%), MRI 3,627 (−49%), X-ray 30,425 (−38%), and CT scans 1,496 (−16%). Radiodiagnostic utilization data are presented in Table 5. Additional descriptive findings Complementary and Alternative Medicine, i.e., AYUSH OPD services experienced the highest proportional decline in attendance (~92%), followed by allied health services such as Dietetics (~84%). While the gender distribution of admissions remained the same across the two study periods, mortality proportions indicated relatively higher male mortality during the COVID-19 period. The total number of in-hospital deaths increased from 590 during 2019-2020 to 1,006 during 2020-2021. Correspondingly, the crude proportion of in-hospital deaths relative to total admissions increased from approximately 2.8% to 6.4%, respectively. These figures represent unadjusted institutional proportions and should be interpreted cautiously because patient-level case-mix and clinical severity data were unavailable. Departmental variations in bed occupancy were observed during the study periods. These variations suggest that changes in inpatient utilization were not uniform across clinical services. However, the present analysis was not designed to establish a formal interaction between department and study period. Discussion In this retrospective record-based pre- vs. post-analysis, hospital service utilization at a tertiary care institute in central India was found to have declined substantially during the COVID-19 pandemic compared with the period just before it. Inpatient admissions, outpatient attendance, and OT facility utilization showed marked reductions, while inpatient mortality and ALOS increased. Laboratory workloads demonstrated a significant shift towards microbiology services, reflecting the diagnostic demands during the pandemic period. The observed reductions in BOR and BTR, alongside a statistically significantly increased ALOS, indicate altered inpatient throughput during the COVID-19 period. Fewer patients were admitted and discharged during the study period, while those who required hospitalization remained admitted for longer durations. This pattern is consistent with higher clinical acuity among admitted indoor patients, reallocation of beds for COVID-19-related wards, and potential delays in presentation or referral for non-COVID-19 conditions. Department-level analysis demonstrated significant heterogeneity in bed occupancy across services, suggesting that the impact of the pandemic varied according to service and facility characteristics. Departments providing emergency, respiratory, or critical care services maintained relatively higher utilization, whereas elective-oriented specialty practices experienced greater declines. The variation in bed occupancy across clinical departments indicates that the changes in inpatient service utilization were heterogeneous. Such differences may reflect variations in service-specific demand, institutional resource allocation, and pandemic-related reorganization of hospital services. records.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Monday, November 23, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health TMPRSS2 Protease Impairs Antibody Recognition of the SARS-CoV-2 Spike Protein by November 17, 2026 in Biology, Health Reading Time: 2 mins read 0 TMPRSS2 Protease Impairs Antibody Recognition of the SARS-CoV-2 Spike Protein Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram The host serine protease TMPRSS2 impairs antibody binding to the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein, according to research examining the immunological impact of this viral entry cofactor. Although TMPRSS2 is well established as a core factor that cleaves the viral spike to initiate cellular fusion during entry, whether the protease influences the humoral immune response against the spike had previously remained poorly characterized. In experiments evaluating spike-expressing and infected cells, TMPRSS2 expression significantly decreased the binding of monoclonal antibodies as well as immune serum. Furthermore, the presence of the active protease decreased the induction of antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity, showing that TMPRSS2 blunts critical antibody-mediated immune recognition on the surface of infected host cells. Discover more Read Med Journals Get Rapid Tests Find Lung Care To pinpoint which regions of the viral spike are altered by this enzymatic activity, investigators screened a panel of 39 monoclonal antibodies directed against diverse spike domains. This profiling revealed that monoclonal antibodies specifically binding to the S2 subunit are the most affected by TMPRSS2 expression among all targeted viral epitopes. Discover more Study Biology Order DNA Kits Study Chemistry Check Symptoms Mechanistically, TMPRSS2 promotes a partial shedding of the S1 subunit and changes the conformation of the S2 subunit. This cleavage reduces binding to the host Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme 2 receptor while simultaneously increasing cell-cell fusion. Moreover, this capacity to diminish antibody recognition is conserved across coronaviruses and shared with other TMPRSS family proteins. In contrast, TMPRSS2 expression in infected cells does not significantly impact virion infectivity or virion antibody recognition, as determined by flow virometry measurements. Taken together, these findings indicate that TMPRSS2 processing of the viral spike favors a distinct structural conformation that is significantly less sensitive to antibody recognition. records.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Monday, November 23, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Nationwide Survey Shows Chinese Quality of Life Rebounded After Omicron Wave by November 21, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 3 mins read 0 Nationwide Survey Shows Chinese Quality of Life Rebounded After Omicron Wave Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram A nationwide investigation in mainland China found that population health-related quality of life dropped sharply during the initial surge of Omicron infections before rebounding in subsequent months. Following the substantial relaxation of nationwide COVID-19 pandemic restrictions, average health-related quality of life scores were markedly lower during the initial outbreak period than in two later follow-up intervals. Researchers observed that while quality of life improved notably after the first wave of infections, measurements remained relatively stable between the second and third survey windows. The study examined public health outcomes following China’s major policy transition on December 7, 2022, which substantially relaxed existing COVID-19 control measures and marked a formal departure from the country’s dynamic zero-COVID policy. This decisive policy change prompted an immediate and rapid nationwide surge in Omicron variant infections across the population. In light of these sweeping changes, the research team sought to evaluate and compare population-level health-related quality of life across three distinct timeframes and examine the specific determinants associated with health utility indices throughout each successive phase. Discover more COVID-19 Omicron COVID-19, Omicron Track Outbreaks To capture health fluctuations over time, investigators conducted three independent cross-sectional surveys across mainland China, gathering data from a total of 2,406 participants. The first survey took place from December 21, 2022, to January 5, 2023, during the height of the policy adjustment and initial infection spike. The second evaluation was administered between January 14 and February 13, 2023, and the third round occurred from May 23 to June 4, 2023. Different participants were recruited across each of the three survey rounds utilizing a snowball sampling methodology. Discover more Learn Sociology COVID-19 COVID Get Rapid Tests Health-related quality of life was evaluated using two standardized assessment instruments: the EQ-5D-5L index and the EQ visual analogue scale, commonly referred to as EQ-VAS. To determine statistical differences across the three observation periods, the authors implemented Kruskal-Wallis tests complemented by pairwise Mann-Whitney U tests. Furthermore, investigators applied period-specific two-part regression models, incorporating logistic regression to examine participants reporting full health with an index of one versus less than full health with an index below one, alongside gamma-log generalized linear models to analyze health disutility among respondents scoring below full health. The resulting measurements demonstrated significant improvements in health status across the evaluated intervals. Among the 2,406 total respondents, mean EQ-5D-5L index scores rose from 0.838 in the first survey period to 0.922 in the second period and 0.927 in the third period. Concurrently, mean EQ-VAS scores increased from 74.732 during the initial survey window to 81.418 in the second and 81.341 in the third. The proportion of participants reporting full health also expanded considerably, moving from 22.3 percent initially to 47.0 percent in the second timeframe and 53.0 percent in the third, accompanied by fewer reported difficulties across most EQ-5D-5L dimensions. Across all three evaluation periods, respiratory symptoms were identified as the most frequent clinical complaint among participants. The two-part regression analyses revealed that an absence of symptoms was consistently associated with significantly higher odds of reporting full health. In contrast, experiencing a first-time COVID-19 infection was associated with greater health disutility among those with scores below full health. The investigators concluded that population-level quality of life was lowest during the acute post-opening surge, with no significant differences observed between the later periods, highlighting the lasting impact of symptom burden and period-specific dynamics during evolving pandemic environments. records.content_title: COVID-19 and the teenage brain: Why the severity of symptoms may matter
records.content: As the teenage brain undergoes critical developmental changes, researchers examine whether the frequency and severity of past COVID-19 infections are linked to the cognitive skills adolescents rely on in the classroom and everyday life. Study: Adolescents’ COVID-19 history is associated with their cognitive performance. Image Credit: vectorfusionart / Shutterstock In a recent study published in the journal Scientific Reports, researchers investigated the associations between coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) infection history, symptom severity, and cognitive, motor, and psychomotor performance among adolescents, including potential gender differences. Adolescents reporting more severe COVID-19 symptoms scored lower in logical reasoning and numerical ability, with lower verbal scores particularly evident among girls. Neither infection occurrence nor frequency was significantly linked to cognitive performance. The research was conducted by scientists from the Faculty of Psychology at Karl Landsteiner University of Health Sciences, in collaboration with the WKNÖ Educational Information Centre in Austria. Background COVID-19 is caused by severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) and has been linked to cognitive impairment in adults, such as difficulties with memory, attention, and executive function. Its potential effects during adolescence remain less understood. This period of development is characterized by substantial brain restructuring, particularly in the areas responsible for higher-order cognitive functions. Previous research has also identified cognitive difficulties among children and young people following infection. School absences, sleep disturbances, and persistent symptoms such as fatigue may contribute to these difficulties. Further large-scale research using standardized cognitive assessments is needed to clarify these associations and potential gender differences. About the study The researchers conducted a cross-sectional study involving 3,860 adolescents aged 12–16 (mean age: 13.5 years) living in Lower Austria, Austria. Data were collected from April to October 2024 through the Austrian Institute for Economic Development’s vocational information center. Girls accounted for 47.4% of the sample. Participants and their parents provided written informed consent, and the assessments were conducted in German under standardized conditions. Study participants self-reported their COVID-19 history, including whether they had been infected, how often, and the severity of their worst illness. Symptom severity was assessed using a 9-point scale, ranging from mild illness with minimal symptoms to severe illness requiring hospitalization. Cognitive abilities were measured using the Inventory for Testing Cognitive Capabilities (INT), which assessed verbal ability, logical reasoning, numerical ability, visual-spatial ability, and long-term memory. The Motorische Leistungsserie (MLS) assessed fine motor ability by measuring tapping speed, gross and fine finger dexterity, and hand guidance errors. A computerized choice-reaction test was used to evaluate the ability to process information during mentally demanding tasks, with the researchers focusing on errors. This custom assessment had not been independently validated. The researchers used multivariate regression and gradient-boosting machine-learning models to examine associations, identify gender differences, and detect potential nonlinear patterns. The models accounted for age, gender, and school type, and the regression analysis incorporated corrections for multiple statistical comparisons. Study results Among the 3,860 participants, 83.9% reported having experienced at least one SARS-CoV-2 infection. On average, previously infected participants who provided infection counts reported around 1.6 infections. The average symptom severity score among those who rated their symptoms was 2.9 out of 9. The researchers found no significant gender differences in infection prevalence, infection frequency, or symptom severity. The multivariate regression analysis showed that COVID-19 symptom severity was associated with lower performance in logical reasoning, numerical ability, and verbal ability among girls, who served as the reference group in the primary statistical model. For logical reasoning, this relationship did not differ significantly between boys and girls. Lower numerical ability was also associated with increasing symptom severity when both genders were analyzed together. The association appeared considerably weaker among boys, but the gender difference was not statistically significant. Verbal ability demonstrated a gender-specific association. More severe COVID-19 symptoms were linked to lower verbal scores among girls, with a significantly weaker relationship among boys. After cognitive scores were converted to a standardized scale (mean = 100, SD = 15), the estimated differences between the least and most severe symptom courses ranged from approximately 3 to 7 points. The gaps were 5.4 points for reasoning and 2.9 points for numerical ability across boys and girls combined, and 7.2 points for verbal ability among girls. These estimates represent differences in specific cognitive domains rather than measured declines in overall IQ. The authors considered these differences potentially meaningful for adolescents’ cognitive and educational development. The machine-learning analysis largely supported the findings on reasoning and verbal ability. Using gradient boosting and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) values, the researchers identified reasoning, verbal ability, fine finger dexterity, and long-term memory as domains for which symptom severity contributed most to model predictions. Numerical ability followed closely. The models suggested possible nonlinear relationships between symptom severity, fine finger dexterity, and long-term memory, but neither outcome showed statistically significant associations in the linear regression models. In particular, fine finger dexterity appeared to deteriorate at the upper end of the severity scale. These exploratory findings need confirmation. After accounting for demographic and educational variables, COVID-19-related factors explained less than an additional 1% of the variation in each performance outcome. The primary regression analysis found no significant links between symptom severity and motor or psychomotor abilities. Additional sensitivity analyses identified logical reasoning as the ability most consistently linked to symptom severity. After excluding participants with the highest severity ratings (7 or above), the association with reasoning remained statistically significant. The association with numerical ability and the gender-specific verbal finding no longer met the threshold for statistical significance, but the estimates remained similar. Infection frequency was not significantly associated with any of the ten performance outcomes. Infection occurrence was also unrelated to performance across the ten domains tested in the primary regression analysis. How much cognitive variation did COVID-19 history explain? Percentage of variation in cognitive and fine motor performance explained by demographic, educational and COVID-19-related factors. Interpretation: COVID-19-related predictors explained less than 1% of the variation in each performance outcome after accounting for demographic and educational factors. Note: The additional COVID-19 contribution represents the percentage-point increase in explained variance, not the percentage of cognitive ability lost. Minor differences in totals reflect rounding in the original publication. The findings do not establish causality. Six selected performance outcomes are presented. Source: Willinger, D., Wunderl, S., & Stieger, S. (2026). Adolescents’ COVID-19 history is associated with their cognitive performance. Scientific Reports, Table 2. DOI: 10.1038/s41598-026-80578-y. Conclusion The findings suggest that adolescents experiencing more severe COVID-19 symptoms may perform less well in certain cognitive domains, particularly reasoning and numerical skills, with lower verbal ability specifically associated with symptom severity among girls. Systemic inflammation and disruption of developing neural networks are possible explanations, but the study did not investigate these mechanisms directly. The cross-sectional design, self-reported infection histories, and lack of pre-infection cognitive assessments prevent causal conclusions. Pre-existing differences in cognitive ability or related factors could also have contributed to more severe illness. The researchers lacked precise infection dates, vaccination histories, and information on pre-existing health conditions, pubertal development, and detailed socioeconomic circumstances. School closures, social isolation, and mental health difficulties may also have influenced cognitive performance. The researchers called for longitudinal studies and confirmation in independent international populations to establish whether these associations reflect lasting effects of infection. Further investigations should also examine the underlying biological processes, factors that may make some adolescents more vulnerable, and effective interventions. Identifying cognitive difficulties following more severe infections may help adolescents receive appropriate educational and developmental support. - Willinger, D., Wunderl, S., & Stieger, S. (2026). Adolescents’ COVID-19 history is associated with their cognitive performance. Scientific Reports. DOI: 10.1038/s41598-026-80578-y, https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-026-80578-y

“畅读会员”点此登录查看原文链接 Research Open access ## 摘要### 背景评估COVID-19肺炎与非COVID病毒性肺炎的胸部CT特征,并评价放射科医师及基于人工智能的系统在区分二者方面的诊断效能。### 方法本回顾性研究纳入181例患者(101例COVID-19,80例非COVID)。胸部CT图像由两名对临床资料和PCR数据设盲的放射科医师独立评估。CT检查同时由深度学习AI算法进行分析。采用单因素和多因素logistic回归比较两组间的CT特征。采用kappa统计量计算两名观察者之间以及AI与COVID-19 RT-PCR检测结果之间的一致性。### 结果两组患者的年龄和性别差异均无统计学意义。外周分布、结节状磨玻璃影和crazy-paving征(铺路石征)在COVID-19病例中显著更常见(*p* < 0.001)。在181例CT检查中,因运动伪影影响肺容积>20%而排除12例(6.6%)后,169例纳入AI分析。AI算法的敏感度为60%,特异度为83.8%(κ = 0.414)。放射科医师之间的观察者一致性几乎达到完美(κ = 0.834),两名放射科医师的判断与PCR结果均具有较强一致性(κ = 0.777和0.700)。存在外周分布、结节状GGO和crazy-paving征,以及不伴肺叶实变、支气管壁增厚、上肺叶优势和树芽征结节,可能提示COVID-19肺炎,其敏感度为91%,特异度为88%。多因素分析中若干比值比的置信区间较宽,反映出受样本量有限的影响,估计精度不高。### 结论外周分布、结节状磨玻璃影和crazy-paving征等提示性CT特征,可能有助于鉴别COVID-19与非COVID病毒性肺炎。尽管AI显示出作为辅助分诊工具的潜力,但放射科医师在诊断准确性和一致性方面表现更佳。上述结果支持将AI作为互补性决策支持系统加以整合,而非在未来应对大流行病的准备工作中将其作为独立的诊断工具。所有性能估计值均来自单中心的内部验证,在获得外部验证之前应视为探索性结果。 打赏 欢迎领取《放射性同位素检测一站式解决方案》领 取 展开全文 开通VIP 享海量文章 全站开放获取+解锁超过 200万篇新闻全文+每日更新 2000+篇,学术前沿动态全时追踪! records.content: 新斯科舍省COVID-19大流行前后中小学生阅读与数学学业成绩变化的性别差异及恢复特征研究 《FACETS》:Pre- and post-COVID-19 outcomes for reading and mathematics in Nova Scotia 【字体: 大 中 小 】 时间:2026年11月21日 来源:FACETS 2.7 为了促进科学的传播,生物通采集了这篇文章 订阅BioHot点这里解锁原文链接推送! “畅读会员”点此登录查看原文链接 Article Open access COVID-19(Coronavirus Disease 2019)大流行导致了广泛的遏制措施,包括学校关闭。现有累积证据表明,学校关闭导致全球儿童学业成绩显著下降。在本研究中,研究人员报告了对新斯科舍省阅读和数学省级教育评估数据(provincial education assessment data)的横断面分析(cross-sectional analyses),以调查该省男孩和女孩的这些模式。分析显示,与疫情前相比,疫情期间阅读和数学得分较低,且女孩的降幅大于男孩。较低的学习水平持续了数年,并出现了一些恢复到疫情前水平的实例。这些发现显示了疫情在学校关闭期间通过家庭学习努力的情况下对儿童学习结果的持久影响。少数恢复到疫情前水平的实例显示了重新获得学习势头的可能性。这两项发现都凸显了学校和老师在支持全面参与社会和经济所需的学业成绩方面的明确价值。 COVID-19(Coronavirus Disease 2019,2019冠状病毒病)疫情在全球范围内引发了大规模遏制措施,其中学校关闭成为各国普遍采用的防控手段。尽管此类措施对于减缓病毒传播具有必要性,但其对儿童日常规范、同伴互动及关键学习机会造成了显著干扰。现有累积证据已表明,学校关闭与全球儿童学业成绩显著下降相关,这一模式在加拿大亦有体现:国际学生评估项目(Programme for International Student Assessment, PISA)数据已显示加拿大学生在阅读、数学和科学领域出现下滑。然而,加拿大各省在公共卫生决策、学校关闭周数、在家学习支持模式以及病假与口罩等附加干扰政策方面存在广泛差异,这意味着某一省份的研究发现未必能推广至其他省份。新斯科舍省人口约100万,且2020至2024年间因省际与国际移民增长约10%,辖境以农村为主,是考察学习损失(learning loss)的独特场域。该省学校自2020年3月23日起关闭,至2022年3月21日解除所有限制,面授学习平均中断约25周,且全省实施基本一致的防疫限制,为评估疫情对学业的独立影响提供了条件。因此,在省级层面独立考察疫情对学业成绩的影响具有重要意义。 下载【非酒精性脂肪性肝炎(NASH)明星治疗靶点】,获取针对NASH的药物开发的最新进展。 领 取 现有文献关于学习损失的学科分布与性别差异尚未形成一致结论。多数研究表明,疫情后数学成绩降幅大于阅读,汇总效应量显示数学损失约为4至6个月学习量,阅读约为2至3个月,分别相当于半个年级和一个三分之一的年级学习量。性别差异的方向亦不明确:部分研究发现男孩降幅更大,部分发现两性无差异,另有研究观察到意大利学生中女孩阅读损失更严重而男孩数学损失更大。近期一项荟萃分析虽发现女孩在两方面损失均大于男孩,但各研究间的广泛差异提示,性别本身可能并非直接驱动因素,而是多种细微机制在平均意义上产生了有意义的差异。此外,关于学习损失持续时长的问题亦待解决,尽管荟萃分析显示损失幅度随时间推移有所减小,但在疫情后两年多数差异仍然显著。在此背景下,有必要在新斯科舍省这一具有独特人口与政策特征的地区开展研究,以揭示疫情前后学生学业成绩的具体变化模式,特别是针对男孩和女孩的差异及其恢复可能性。 为系统探究上述问题,研究人员利用新斯科舍省全省教育评估数据,对3、6、8和10年级学生在阅读与数学两个学科的疫情前、疫情期间及疫情后学业表现进行了横断面(cross-sectional)比较分析。研究得出三个主要结论:第一,几乎所有年级的阅读和数学成绩在疫情期间均出现显著下降,且数学降幅普遍大于阅读,符合国际研究趋势;第二,女生面临的降幅普遍大于男生,尤其在6、8年级阅读和3、6、8、10年级数学中表现明显,但3年级阅读和10年级阅读呈现例外;第三,学习损失具有持久影响,多数学生成绩在疫情后数年仍未恢复至疫情前水平,但在少数情况下出现了恢复迹象。这些发现不仅凸显了学校与教师面授教学在支持学业成就方面的不可替代价值,也为未来可能的教育中断风险提供了实证依据,提示需重视学生的长期学业支持并探索影响性别差异与恢复机制的具体过程。 本研究的关键技术方法主要依托新斯科舍省2015–2016至2024–2025学年全省学生评估数据,样本队列涵盖Conseil scolaire acadien provincial(CSAP,阿卡德语区域委员会)在内的公立学校学生,数据集共涉及146,396名不同年级被试。研究聚焦阅读与数学两门学科,因两者评分完全自动化且数据相对充分。技术核心在于使用项目反应理论(Item Response Theory, IRT)模型生成θ分数(theta scores),具体为双相3参数Logistic模型(dichotomous 3PL, constant 1.7),采用期望后验估计法(Expected A Posteriori, EAP)与浮动先验,并将原始分缩放至年度省均值500、标准差100的量表(scale)范围(200–800)。数据分析在R环境中完成,包括描述性统计、偏度与峰度检验;针对缺失数据,采用卡方检验(chi-square tests)与Cramér's V效应量评估其与性别及年份的关联;针对年级与评估类型,分别实施年份与性别双因素方差分析(two-way factorial ANOVA, Type III),并以异方差一致性估计(heteroskedasticity-consistent estimators, HC3)校正异方差性问题;通过估计边际均值(estimated marginal means)与Holm调整后的事后两两比较(pairwise comparisons),精确识别疫情前、中、后期之间的均值差异模式。此外,研究使用了人工智能工具辅助数据代码生成与验证,并经人工核查。 **描述性统计与整体方差分析结果显示**,通过计算各年度、各年级量表分的描述性统计量并进行正态性检验(基于偏度与峰度),所有数据均呈正态分布。阅读与数学两科均存在显著的年份主效应(main effects of year),且阅读中所有年级均存在显著的性别主效应(main effects of gender),女生得分显著高于男生;数学中3、6、8年级性别主效应显著,10年级不显著。绝大多数情况下,年份与性别的两向交互作用(two-way interaction)达到显著水平,支持后续分性别进行精细对比。 **疫情前与疫情期间的对比结果方面**,阅读领域,3年级男生和女生在2018–2019学年的得分均显著高于2021–2022学年,而2022–2023学年与前期无显著差异;6、8、10年级女生疫情前得分显著高于疫情期间,而男生表现不一致,6、10年级多无显著差异,8年级除一年外均显著下降。数学领域,几乎所有年级女生疫情前得分均显著高于疫情期间;男生则呈现大部分对比显著下降,但每个年级均有1至2个对比未达显著水平。 **疫情期间与疫情后的对比结果显示**,阅读方面,3年级学生从2021–2022至2023–2024学年成绩显著上升;6、8年级女生成绩在期间与后期无显著变化;10年级女生后期得分反而显著低于期间;男生各年级期间与后期多无显著差异。数学方面,3、6年级女生和男生在后期成绩显著高于期间;8年级男生无显著变化;10年级仅一个对比显示男生后期显著上升。 **疫情前与疫情后女生和男生的对比结果(恢复情况)显示**,阅读方面,3年级男女生疫情前与疫情后均无显著差异,提示已恢复至前期水平;6、8、10年级女生疫情后仍显著低于疫情前;男生仅6、8年级各有一个对比显示长期损失。数学方面,3年级男女生成绩后期反超前期;6、8、10年级女生仍显著低于前期;男生6、10年级相似,8年级显著高于前期,提示存在恢复。 讨论部分指出,本研究结果与国际文献一致,确认了疫情对阅读和数学成绩的负面影响,且数学降幅大于阅读,原因可能在于阅读作为课外愉悦活动具有一定保护效应。性别差异方面,女生损失更大的模式与近期荟萃分析一致,但3年级阅读和10年级阅读的例外提示早期阅读教学阶段可能受性别差异影响较小,而高年级阅读可能因长期累积效应呈现不同模式。研究人员指出,广泛观察到的性别差异提示背后可能存在多重细微机制,如女生在疫情期间可能面临更高压力反应、同伴互动减少,或具备更强的自我调节与学校参与优势,这些机制需在未来研究中直接检验。关于持续时间,多数损失长期存在,但少数恢复案例(尤其因数据涵盖2023–2024至2024–2025学年,距离疫情较远)尤为可贵,显示出儿童、教师与教育系统的韧性。研究同时承认局限:横断面设计无法追踪个体纵向变化,且2020至2024年间新斯科舍省因移民导致人口增长约10%,加之评估参与政策的排除标准限制了结果的外推性。 综上所述,新斯科舍省3、6、8、10年级学生在阅读和数学两个学科的全省评估数据提供了广泛且明确的证据,表明COVID-19疫情后学生学业成绩出现显著下降,其中女生所受影响关联大于男生。学习损失持续多年,但在部分情况下显示回升至疫情前水平的迹象。这些学业结果的庞大且持久的影响,凸显了在疫情等特殊时期支持学生学业的重要性;与此同时,部分学业恢复的证据也展现了儿童、教师与教育系统的韧性。 records.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Monday, November 23, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Biology Computational Workflow Optimizes Nanobody Binding Using Sequence Models and Molecular Simulations by November 21, 2026 in Biology Reading Time: 6 mins read 0 Computational Workflow Optimizes Nanobody Binding Using Sequence Models and Molecular Simulations Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram A computational antibody engineering pipeline coupling a pretrained nanobody language model with structure-based binding free energy prediction and all-atom molecular dynamics improves the discovery of higher-affinity single-domain antibodies against viral antigens without requiring initial target-specific model training. Described by researchers in Genome Biology, the open-access workflow, designated LmPro-Nano, addresses long-standing bottlenecks in nanobody affinity maturation, where experimental screening remains resource-intensive and conventional computational pipelines often obscure the distinct contributions of individual design stages. Nanobodies, which represent the single variable heavy-chain domains derived from camelid heavy-chain-only antibodies, offer distinctive advantages over conventional immunoglobulins due to their low molecular weight, extended third complementarity-determining regions, distinctive framework architectures, and convex paratopes capable of accessing recessed epitopes. By evaluating each computational module against independent empirical benchmarks, the study demonstrates that sequence-driven localization of antigen-binding residues and geometric free-energy scoring can enrich candidate libraries for tighter binders across clinically relevant coronavirus targets, including the receptor-binding domain of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2. The structural motivation for specialized single-domain computational design stems from the distinctive molecular characteristics of camelid heavy-chain fragments. However, the rapid emergence of viral escape variants, such as the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron lineage JN.1 that predominated during the investigation, creates an urgent operational demand for design workflows that can be rapidly redeployed directly on updated antigen sequences without redesigning therapeutic scaffolds from scratch. While diverse computational methodologies have emerged—spanning iterative graph neural networks, equivariant sequence-structure generators, and inverse folding protocols—they frequently evaluate candidates purely by sequence recovery against native backbones, which conflates sequence memorization with physical binding improvement and leaves the isolated impact of individual pipeline components unresolved. Discover more Try Sim Games simulations Simulations To overcome this limitation, the authors structured LmPro-Nano around an architectural core called Lm-Nano, a foundational nanobody language model whose encoder is frozen after dual-phase training. The initial pretraining phase exposed the model to unpaired nanobody sequences obtained from the Integrated Nanobody Database for Immunoinformatics, masking amino acid residues exclusively across the three CDR loops while preserving framework positions. To preserve length transferability, the transformer encoder incorporates multi-head attention equipped with rotary position embeddings, which calculate attention weights based on relative residue separation rather than fixed coordinate indices. Following masked-language pretraining, Lm-Nano underwent structural fine-tuning on protein complexes cataloged in the nanobody subset of the Structural Antibody Database, termed SAbDab-Nano, to impart antigen-conditioned representations. The resulting frozen encoder subsequently powers two distinct functional heads: a generative decoder built from three residual multilayer perceptron layers designed to propose CDR3 sequences alongside coarse-to-fine loop conformations, and a paratope classification head trained to assign per-residue binding probabilities across the entire domain using nanobody and antigen sequences alone. Discover more Study Biology Study Chemistry Track Biotech Try Flight Sims Downstream candidate selection in LmPro-Nano relies on ProFE-Net, a specialized neural network formulated to predict the change in Gibbs free energy of binding resulting from single amino acid substitutions. A residue-level fusion module combines these representations, processing wild-type and mutant sequences over shared backbone coordinates in both forward and inverted orientations to enforce mathematical anti-symmetry. Benchmark evaluations on 4,947 single-point mutations derived from the RDE-PPI complex dataset revealed that combining ProFE-Net with the geometric baseline RDE-Net at an uncalibrated equal weighting yielded superior rank correlation and reduced prediction error compared to either model operating independently, providing a robust metric for prioritizing candidate variants before conducting explicit-solvent simulations. The generative loop redesign capacity of the workflow was evaluated on 3-2A2-4, a therapeutic nanobody known to neutralize diverse sarbecoviruses and Omicron subvariants whose crystallographic structure in complex with the ancestral SARS-CoV-2 receptor-binding domain had been resolved under Protein Data Bank accession code 7X2L. When tasked with redesigning the CDR3 loop across an iterated best-of-N resampling cycle filtered by strict biophysical and naturalness thresholds, Lm-Nano proposed an optimized variant carrying three coordinated substitutions: E95N, N96Y, and F100G, converting the parental loop sequence LENGGFFYY into LNYGGFGYY. Notably, the chosen candidate exhibited the joint-highest generator perplexity in the elite sampling pool, demonstrating that candidate selection was governed by downstream energetic screening rather than sequence likelihood memorization. The structural stability and energetic affinity of this redesigned loop were subsequently interrogated across multiple evolutionary backgrounds, providing a rigorous test of the model’s generalizability against divergent viral targets. To assess the physical consequences of the redesigned 3-2A2-4 loop, the authors performed all-atom explicit-solvent molecular dynamics simulations of both parental and mutated complexes in duplicate 500-nanosecond trajectories across three distinct receptor-binding domains: the ancestral strain, BA.2.86, and JN.1. Energetic analysis using molecular mechanics/Poisson–Boltzmann surface area and generalized Born surface area methods indicated consistent thermodynamic stabilization for the optimized variant over the most settled 50-nanosecond segment of each trajectory, recording favorable binding energy increments of 3.60 kilojoules per mole under MM/PBSA and 1.88 kilojoules per mole under MM/GBSA. Component decomposition revealed that this gain was driven primarily by favorable desolvation rather than increased direct contact interactions; the engineered variant sacrificed 184 kilojoules per mole in electrostatic interaction energy and 16 kilojoules per mole in van der Waals contacts, but compensated by paying 199 kilojoules per mole less in polar solvation penalty. This thermodynamic shift coincided with the removal of an apex carboxylate group via the E95N substitution, allowing an adjacent lysine residue to form stable interface salt bridges, shifting contact frequency from 0.008 to 0.212. The localization capability of LmPro-Nano was independently tested on VHH72, a nanobody directed against the receptor-binding domain for which comprehensive deep mutational scanning data were available. By leveraging AlphaSeq empirical binding affinities encompassing 1,579 single substitutions across 89 positions, the research team could benchmark computational predictions against quantitative experimental values without prior training contamination. Given only the primary sequence of VHH72 and the receptor-binding domain, the frozen Lm-Nano paratope head scored all 125 positions of the nanobody without restricting its focus to canonical CDR loops. The top 17 predicted positions captured 13 of the 17 structurally verified interface residues within an 8-angstrom C-beta distance threshold, achieving a per-position area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.9771. Framework residues contributed substantially to the localized binding interface, reflecting the functional enlargement of framework region 2 characteristic of single-domain antibodies in the absence of light-chain pairing. Following interface localization, the team exhaustively enumerated all 18 non-parental amino acid substitutions across the 17 identified positions, yielding 306 candidates, of which 305 possessed empirical binding measurements. Ranking these candidates with the combined ProFE-Net and RDE-Net scoring ensemble identified a top-ten candidate panel in which seven variants exhibited higher experimental binding affinities than the parental clone, representing a 2.57-fold enrichment over the baseline rate of the candidate pool. The highest-ranked candidate, a framework substitution designated T61Y, yielded the largest empirical affinity gain in the dataset, enhancing binding by 2.92 kilojoules per mole and conferring an affinity 3.2 times greater than parental VHH72. Crucially, when the same scoring ensemble was applied across all 1,579 mutational records without the sequence-only paratope gate, only two of the top ten candidates bound more tightly than parental wild-type, demonstrating that sequence-based paratope localization serves as a vital gating filter to exclude non-interface artifacts that energy scoring functions alone fail to penalize. The ten prioritized VHH72 variants, alongside parental VHH72 and a neutral control substitution designated G42I, were subjected to rigorous molecular dynamics characterization involving 36 independent 500-nanosecond trajectories modeled using the CHARMM36 force field and explicit TIP3P solvent. Trajectory analysis over the most stable 50-nanosecond windows demonstrated that eight of the ten designs achieved more favorable binding enthalpies under MM/PBSA than the parental complex, with a paired mean shift of 13.7 kilojoules per mole in the favorable direction. Electrostatic and polar solvation terms exhibited large compensatory shifts of up to 260 and 226 kilojoules per mole, particularly among mutations altering formal charge. MM/GBSA calculations corroborated these findings across compatible dielectric parameters, yielding an average favorable shift of 15.7 kilojoules per mole. The simulations confirmed that physical modeling in explicit solvent provides effective within-position discrimination, refining candidate prioritization where heuristic energy scores primarily distinguish between residue positions rather than subtle amino acid variations. To evaluate broader applicability beyond coronavirus antigens, the investigators tested ProFE-Net and the ensemble scorer on external surface plasmon resonance binding datasets covering green fluorescent protein, tumor necrosis factor alpha, and interleukin-23 complexes. On the green fluorescent protein variant panel, the equal-weight ensemble achieved the highest rank correlation among tested models, while standalone ProFE-Net proved superior on cytokine complexes, capturing the tightest-binding variant in one cytokine panel where comparative baselines failed. The authors note, however, that current implementations rely on surrogate energy scoring and simulated structural ensembles, necessitating future wet-lab experimental campaigns to validate fully prospective designs across broader non-viral targets, including G protein-coupled receptors. Overall, LmPro-Nano establishes a modular, verifiable paradigm for antibody engineering, showing that coupling sequence-only language models with physical energy scoring offers a practical route toward rapid, targeted nanobody affinity optimization.
